A month before, it was worth about five point four trillion dollars,

20
00:00:58,914 --> 00:01:3,192
roughly eight cents of every dollar in the whole S&P five hundred.

21
00:01:3,212 --> 00:01:8,364
If you own a plain index fund, the safe, boring kind everyone recommends,

22
00:01:8,384 --> 00:01:10,396
you own a lot of Nvidia.

23
00:01:10,416 --> 00:01:15,528
Add the rest of the Magnificent Seven, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet,

24
00:01:15,548 --> 00:01:16,860
Meta and Tesla,

25
00:01:16,880 --> 00:01:19,020
and about thirty-five dollars of every

26
00:01:19,040 --> 00:01:22,270
hundred in that fund sits on seven companies.

27
00:01:22,290 --> 00:01:23,462
I'm diversified.

28
00:01:23,482 --> 00:01:25,242
Five hundred companies.

29
00:01:25,262 --> 00:01:28,304
Seven of them are a third of the pie.

30
00:01:28,324 --> 00:01:30,542
...That is a big slice.

31
00:01:30,562 --> 00:01:34,694
Even at the dot-com peak, the market wasn't this lopsided.

32
00:01:34,714 --> 00:01:37,778
And most of those giants are betting on the same thing.

33
00:01:37,798 --> 00:01:39,790
That bet is expensive.

34
00:01:39,810 --> 00:01:40,590
This year,

35
00:01:40,610 --> 00:01:45,550
the four biggest cloud companies plan to spend over seven hundred billion dollars

36
00:01:45,570 --> 00:01:46,902
building data centers.

37
00:01:46,922 --> 00:01:49,086
Next year, more than a trillion.

38
00:01:49,106 --> 00:01:52,098
The biggest line on that shopping list says Nvidia,

39
00:01:52,118 --> 00:01:55,530
whose last quarter brought in ninety-six billion dollars,

40
00:01:55,550 --> 00:01:58,240
more than double the year before.

41
00:01:59,263 --> 00:02:3,422
By late October, investors were staring at four cracks.

42
00:02:3,442 --> 00:02:6,146
Crack one: the money goes in a circle.

43
00:02:6,166 --> 00:02:8,758
Nvidia invests in its own customers,

44
00:02:8,778 --> 00:02:12,950
the AI labs and chip-rental firms that then buy Nvidia chips.

45
00:02:12,970 --> 00:02:16,482
It owns a stake in CoreWeave, which rents those chips out,

46
00:02:16,502 --> 00:02:21,202
and agreed to buy up to six point three billion dollars of the computing power

47
00:02:21,222 --> 00:02:22,554
CoreWeave can't sell.

48
00:02:22,574 --> 00:02:27,546
Nvidia's own finance chief knows how that sounds: "we know some will call this

49
00:02:27,566 --> 00:02:29,069
circular financing."

50
00:02:29,089 --> 00:02:31,415
Here's a few billion dollars.

51
00:02:31,435 --> 00:02:32,227
Wow!

52
00:02:32,247 --> 00:02:34,277
What should I spend it on?

53
00:02:34,297 --> 00:02:35,519
Funny you should ask.

54
00:02:35,539 --> 00:02:38,223
Crack two: the chips are the collateral.

55
00:02:38,243 --> 00:02:42,867
Firms like CoreWeave borrowed huge sums to buy chips, rented them out,

56
00:02:42,887 --> 00:02:45,479
and pledged those same chips to borrow more.

57
00:02:45,499 --> 00:02:50,411
At one point CoreWeave owed over five dollars for every dollar of equity.

58
00:02:50,431 --> 00:02:53,103
Fine, while a used chip holds its value.

59
00:02:53,123 --> 00:02:56,635
But Nvidia brings out a new generation every year or two,

60
00:02:56,655 --> 00:02:59,567
and each one makes the last one worth less.

61
00:02:59,587 --> 00:03:2,219
And Michael Burry, who called the housing crash,

62
00:03:2,239 --> 00:03:6,131
says the giants book their servers as lasting longer than they do,

63
00:03:6,151 --> 00:03:7,552
which flatters profits.

64
00:03:7,572 --> 00:03:10,144
The nightmare: one borrower misses one

65
00:03:10,164 --> 00:03:12,888
payment, the lender grabs the chips to sell,

66
00:03:12,908 --> 00:03:17,480
and everyone learns that afternoon what a used AI chip is worth in a hurry.

67
00:03:17,500 --> 00:03:18,632
It hasn't happened.

68
00:03:18,652 --> 00:03:21,167
But every chip investor has thought about it.

69
00:03:21,187 --> 00:03:23,151
Crack three: who's paying.

70
00:03:23,171 --> 00:03:24,443
By the end of July,

71
00:03:24,463 --> 00:03:29,563
Nvidia was owed about sixty-three billion dollars for chips it had shipped but not

72
00:03:29,583 --> 00:03:30,755
been paid for yet.

73
00:03:30,775 --> 00:03:35,519
And this year, just three buyers made up more than two fifths of its sales.

74
00:03:35,539 --> 00:03:40,279
Picture a restaurant where three tables order two of every five plates,

75
00:03:40,299 --> 00:03:42,293
and a lot of the food goes on a tab.

76
00:03:42,313 --> 00:03:44,037
Crack four: the plug.

77
00:03:44,057 --> 00:03:45,309
You can buy a chip.

78
00:03:45,329 --> 00:03:48,061
You can't buy electricity that doesn't exist.

79
00:03:48,081 --> 00:03:51,593
In northern Virginia, the data-center capital of the world,

80
00:03:51,613 --> 00:03:56,456
the wait to hook a new building up to the grid had stretched to about seven years.

81
00:03:56,476 --> 00:03:59,800
And the power that does exist, somebody pays for.

82
00:03:59,820 --> 00:04:3,352
On America's biggest grid, across thirteen states,

83
00:04:3,372 --> 00:04:8,436
power plants get paid just to stand ready, and families cover that in their bills.

84
00:04:8,456 --> 00:04:10,488
Then the data centers piled in.

85
00:04:10,508 --> 00:04:15,048
Households there were paying an estimated twenty-five to thirty dollars a month more

86
00:04:15,068 --> 00:04:20,730
than in twenty twenty-four, and the grid's own watchdog blamed data centers first.

87
00:04:21,278 --> 00:04:23,443
Why is the electric bill up again?

88
00:04:23,463 --> 00:04:24,808
Hi, neighbor!

89
00:04:24,828 --> 00:04:27,060
Nobody reads a spending report.

90
00:04:27,080 --> 00:04:28,872
Everybody reads their power bill.

91
00:04:28,892 --> 00:04:29,753
Hold that thought.

92
00:04:29,773 --> 00:04:31,985
Wall Street had its own bad news.

93
00:04:32,005 --> 00:04:36,237
On October twenty-ninth, Google had its worst trading day ever.

94
00:04:36,257 --> 00:04:41,121
The next day Intel fell by a quarter, chip stocks slid into a bear market,

95
00:04:41,141 --> 00:04:44,718
and Apple, the boring one, passed Nvidia in value.

96
00:04:44,738 --> 00:04:46,398
By the second of November,

97
00:04:46,418 --> 00:04:51,638
the forty-seven biggest AI and chip stocks had lost about five trillion dollars

98
00:04:51,658 --> 00:04:52,430
since the top.

99
00:04:52,450 --> 00:04:55,282
That's about what the whole dot-com crash wiped out,

100
00:04:55,302 --> 00:04:57,594
and that took two and a half years.

101
00:04:57,614 --> 00:04:59,686
This took four weeks.

102
00:04:59,706 --> 00:05:1,916
Then came the election.

103
00:05:2,899 --> 00:05:5,511
Tuesday, the third of November.

104
00:05:5,531 --> 00:05:7,023
Democrats won the House.

105
00:05:7,043 --> 00:05:8,264
Then they won the Senate.

106
00:05:8,284 --> 00:05:10,904
Further down the ballot, in ten states,

107
00:05:10,924 --> 00:05:14,036
there were forty-one local votes on data centers.

108
00:05:14,056 --> 00:05:16,248
Voters went against them in forty.

109
00:05:16,268 --> 00:05:18,360
Twenty-one of those were in Ohio.

110
00:05:18,380 --> 00:05:21,906
The one town that said yes was Harwood, North Dakota.

111
00:05:21,926 --> 00:05:23,778
Ohio, no.

112
00:05:23,798 --> 00:05:25,330
Ohio, no.

113
00:05:25,350 --> 00:05:26,902
Ohio, no.

114
00:05:26,922 --> 00:05:27,752
Ohio...

115
00:05:27,772 --> 00:05:28,472
Hi!

116
00:05:28,492 --> 00:05:29,192
Yes!

117
00:05:29,212 --> 00:05:30,037
Over here!

118
00:05:30,057 --> 00:05:32,921
That's the power bill, showing up at the ballot box.

119
00:05:32,941 --> 00:05:36,081
In Ohio, Sherrod Brown beat Jon Husted,

120
00:05:36,101 --> 00:05:40,833
who'd been called "the face of data centers." In Texas, Elon Musk,

121
00:05:40,853 --> 00:05:44,873
the cycle's biggest donor with at least four hundred and seventy-four million

122
00:05:44,893 --> 00:05:47,337
dollars, lost both big races.

123
00:05:47,357 --> 00:05:48,606
His reaction:

124
00:05:48,626 --> 00:05:52,185
Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now.

125
00:05:52,205 --> 00:05:54,957
Here's why a town vote moves Wall Street.

126
00:05:54,977 --> 00:05:59,993
A data center needs land, power and a permit, and all three are local.

127
00:06:0,013 --> 00:06:2,233
Goldman Sachs figured moratoriums like

128
00:06:2,253 --> 00:06:4,993
these could hit about forty-five percent of

129
00:06:5,013 --> 00:06:7,310
America's planned data-center expansion.

130
00:06:7,330 --> 00:06:9,642
And the bigger fear was Washington.

131
00:06:9,662 --> 00:06:13,154
For years, AI was mostly left alone to build.

132
00:06:13,174 --> 00:06:18,626
Now a Democratic Congress, elected the same night voters said no to data centers,

133
00:06:18,646 --> 00:06:22,570
might want rules on where data centers go, who pays for their power,

134
00:06:22,590 --> 00:06:24,622
and how fast the build-out runs.

135
00:06:24,642 --> 00:06:31,136
One congressman, Robert Garcia, had two words for AI executives: "Lawyer up."

136
00:06:32,700 --> 00:06:33,431
So.

137
00:06:33,451 --> 00:06:35,501
Data centers.

138
00:06:35,607 --> 00:06:36,824
We were just leaving.

139
00:06:36,844 --> 00:06:38,496
No rule has passed.

140
00:06:38,516 --> 00:06:39,408
Not one.

141
00:06:39,428 --> 00:06:41,900
It was the fear of a rule that did the selling.

142
00:06:41,920 --> 00:06:46,652
That trillion-dollar shopping list had picked up some small print: if they let us

143
00:06:46,672 --> 00:06:48,122
build it.

144
00:06:49,113 --> 00:06:52,097
And on Wednesday, Wall Street partied anyway.

145
00:06:52,117 --> 00:06:56,889
The Dow jumped fifteen hundred and sixty-nine points, about three percent,

146
00:06:56,909 --> 00:07:0,541
its best day after a midterm since nineteen eighty-two,

147
00:07:0,561 --> 00:07:2,853
and oil fell more than nine percent.

148
00:07:2,873 --> 00:07:4,825
Traders loved the cheap oil.

149
00:07:4,845 --> 00:07:6,737
They hadn't gotten to the new Congress yet.

150
00:07:6,757 --> 00:07:8,610
The party lasted one day.

151
00:07:8,630 --> 00:07:13,450
That morning, Vice President JD Vance had posted on X.

152
00:07:13,470 --> 00:07:15,552
The reason we lost is the war.

153
00:07:15,572 --> 00:07:17,104
The war with Iran.

154
00:07:17,124 --> 00:07:20,056
That raised hopes of a deal, and oil fell.

155
00:07:20,076 --> 00:07:24,013
By Thursday morning, traders doubted it, and oil climbed again.

156
00:07:24,033 --> 00:07:28,277
Then, before the opening bell, Reuters dropped the next problem.

157
00:07:28,297 --> 00:07:33,549
About six hundred thousand of Nvidia's H200 chips were sitting in Hong Kong,

158
00:07:33,569 --> 00:07:35,566
waiting for Beijing to let them in.

159
00:07:35,586 --> 00:07:39,338
Washington had cleared the sales last winter, case by case,

160
00:07:39,358 --> 00:07:41,290
with a twenty-five percent tariff.

161
00:07:41,310 --> 00:07:44,554
In August, Beijing let companies use them in Hong Kong.

162
00:07:44,574 --> 00:07:46,826
Into mainland China, in bulk?

163
00:07:46,846 --> 00:07:47,889
Still waiting.

164
00:07:47,909 --> 00:07:50,063
You said we can sell them!

165
00:07:50,083 --> 00:07:50,895
You can.

166
00:07:50,915 --> 00:07:52,680
Twenty-five percent, please.

167
00:07:52,700 --> 00:07:53,792
They're in Hong Kong!

168
00:07:53,812 --> 00:07:55,702
Can they come in?

169
00:07:56,506 --> 00:07:57,399
Not yet.

170
00:07:57,419 --> 00:08:2,471
The strange part: Nvidia had already taken a four hundred million dollar hit on

171
00:08:2,491 --> 00:08:4,703
H200s that nobody bought.

172
00:08:4,723 --> 00:08:8,693
And the ones that did have buyers couldn't get through the door.

173
00:08:9,693 --> 00:08:10,645
Nine thirty.

174
00:08:10,665 --> 00:08:12,423
The bell rings in New York.

175
00:08:12,443 --> 00:08:16,455
It takes the Nasdaq six minutes to give back the whole rally.

176
00:08:16,475 --> 00:08:17,707
So much for Wednesday.

177
00:08:17,727 --> 00:08:18,919
Ten thirty-five.

178
00:08:18,939 --> 00:08:23,251
The Nasdaq is down four percent and the Dow seven hundred points.

179
00:08:23,271 --> 00:08:27,903
Across the S&P five hundred, more than two trillion dollars has vanished,

180
00:08:27,923 --> 00:08:31,315
and more than four hundred billion of it is Nvidia alone.

181
00:08:31,335 --> 00:08:35,263
That's about twice Amazon's entire building budget for the year.

182
00:08:35,283 --> 00:08:36,624
Eleven seventeen.

183
00:08:36,644 --> 00:08:41,327
The VIX, Wall Street's fear gauge, is up sixty-five percent.

184
00:08:41,347 --> 00:08:45,350
Think of it as the price of crash insurance, and everybody wants some.

185
00:08:45,370 --> 00:08:46,842
Eleven thirty-seven.

186
00:08:46,862 --> 00:08:52,242
The Dow is on track for its worst second day after a midterm in records going back

187
00:08:52,262 --> 00:08:53,936
to eighteen ninety-six.

188
00:08:53,956 --> 00:08:55,068
One thirty-eight.

189
00:08:55,088 --> 00:09:0,554
AMD's boss, Lisa Su, speaks up, with her stock down fifteen percent.

190
00:09:0,574 --> 00:09:5,230
I think the market can sometimes be a little bit short-sighted.

191
00:09:5,250 --> 00:09:6,392
Aaaaah!

192
00:09:6,412 --> 00:09:7,444
Two fifty-eight.

193
00:09:7,464 --> 00:09:10,060
And this is where ordinary people come in.

194
00:09:10,080 --> 00:09:13,093
Maybe you're at work, checking your phone under the desk.

195
00:09:13,113 --> 00:09:15,964
You own a plain S&P five hundred fund.

196
00:09:15,984 --> 00:09:18,376
If it holds a quarter of a million dollars,

197
00:09:18,396 --> 00:09:23,028
Nvidia alone took about nine hundred and ninety dollars out of it that morning.

198
00:09:23,048 --> 00:09:26,260
By now, small investors have sold, on net,

199
00:09:26,280 --> 00:09:29,492
three hundred and fifty-eight million dollars of stock,

200
00:09:29,512 --> 00:09:31,678
the most since March twenty twenty.

201
00:09:31,698 --> 00:09:33,828
Buy the dip...

202
00:09:34,435 --> 00:09:35,795
...or sell the dip?

203
00:09:35,815 --> 00:09:41,899
Viraj Patel at Vanda Research called it "a total capitulation by retail investors,"

204
00:09:41,919 --> 00:09:44,138
with "no signs of buying the dip."

205
00:09:44,158 --> 00:09:45,310
Three oh six.

206
00:09:45,330 --> 00:09:50,406
Charlie McElligott, a strategist at Nomura, explains who's really selling.

207
00:09:50,426 --> 00:09:51,981
They're shooting the generals.

208
00:09:52,001 --> 00:09:54,753
The generals are the year's biggest winners.

209
00:09:54,773 --> 00:09:59,337
Hedge funds had made a fortune in twenty twenty-six, and with two months to go,

210
00:09:59,357 --> 00:10:1,189
they sold the winners to lock it in.

211
00:10:1,209 --> 00:10:5,621
Computer-driven funds and funds on borrowed money were forced to sell too.

212
00:10:5,641 --> 00:10:7,789
And nobody stepped in to buy.

213
00:10:7,809 --> 00:10:8,701
Great year.

214
00:10:8,721 --> 00:10:9,613
Let's bank it.

215
00:10:9,633 --> 00:10:11,079
Sell the winners.

216
00:10:11,099 --> 00:10:13,058
Which ones?

217
00:10:13,078 --> 00:10:13,830
Yes.

218
00:10:13,850 --> 00:10:17,346
Single-name stock moves are absolutely BONKERS.

219
00:10:17,366 --> 00:10:18,458
Four o'clock.

220
00:10:18,478 --> 00:10:19,628
The closing bell.

221
00:10:19,648 --> 00:10:23,180
The Dow lost eighteen hundred and thirty-three points.

222
00:10:23,200 --> 00:10:25,672
The S&P fell over four percent.

223
00:10:25,692 --> 00:10:30,364
The Nasdaq fell five and a half, its biggest drop in nineteen months,

224
00:10:30,384 --> 00:10:34,348
and is now in a correction, at least ten percent below its high.

225
00:10:34,368 --> 00:10:37,640
Chip stocks had their worst day since March twenty twenty.

226
00:10:37,660 --> 00:10:42,404
Nvidia closed at a hundred and eighty-one dollars, down more than nine percent.

227
00:10:42,424 --> 00:10:46,788
And while everything burned, AppLovin rose almost thirty percent,

228
00:10:46,808 --> 00:10:51,160
and Goldman Sachs picked that day to name a hundred and nine new partners,

229
00:10:51,180 --> 00:10:54,242
its biggest class since twenty ten.

230
00:10:55,409 --> 00:10:56,181
Honestly?

231
00:10:56,201 --> 00:10:58,731
Great day to get promoted.

232
00:10:59,682 --> 00:11:3,394
It's easy to think a crash like this only hurts rich people.

233
00:11:3,414 --> 00:11:4,110
It doesn't.

234
00:11:4,130 --> 00:11:8,022
Around seventy million Americans save in a 401(k),

235
00:11:8,042 --> 00:11:9,914
mostly through the same index funds,

236
00:11:9,934 --> 00:11:13,066
and the pensions of teachers and firefighters hold them too.

237
00:11:13,086 --> 00:11:15,745
When the seven giants fall, they fall too.

238
00:11:15,765 --> 00:11:17,697
It goes deeper than stocks.

239
00:11:17,717 --> 00:11:20,089
Data centers run on borrowed money,

240
00:11:20,109 --> 00:11:22,961
much of it raised from insurers and pension funds.

241
00:11:22,981 --> 00:11:27,601
Pimco bought a big piece of the bonds for Meta's giant Louisiana data center with

242
00:11:27,621 --> 00:11:32,705
savers' money, and Washington has moved to open 401(k)s to this kind of lending.

243
00:11:32,725 --> 00:11:37,166
So your retirement may be quietly lending to a half-built building.

244
00:11:37,186 --> 00:11:40,770
And some get hit without owning a share: the electricians,

245
00:11:40,790 --> 00:11:45,582
some making two hundred and sixty thousand dollars a year on data-center jobs,

246
00:11:45,602 --> 00:11:47,394
and the diners that feed them.

247
00:11:47,414 --> 00:11:49,326
Thursday didn't stop that work.

248
00:11:49,346 --> 00:11:52,581
But if the spending stops, it lands there first.

249
00:11:52,601 --> 00:11:55,573
If you're twenty-five, Thursday was a sale.

250
00:11:55,593 --> 00:12:1,163
If you're sixty-two and retiring in the spring, it was a very long day.

251
00:12:2,242 --> 00:12:4,234
So who do you get angry at?

252
00:12:4,254 --> 00:12:6,126
Every crash wants a villain.

253
00:12:6,146 --> 00:12:7,858
Twenty oh eight had the banks.

254
00:12:7,878 --> 00:12:10,158
Thursday doesn't really have one.

255
00:12:10,178 --> 00:12:12,244
I just didn't want the bill.

256
00:12:12,264 --> 00:12:14,538
I just wanted to keep my good year.

257
00:12:14,558 --> 00:12:16,653
I just said not yet.

258
00:12:16,673 --> 00:12:18,417
I just sold chips!

259
00:12:18,437 --> 00:12:21,289
Every one of those choices made sense on its own.

260
00:12:21,309 --> 00:12:23,598
They just all landed on the same morning.

261
00:12:23,618 --> 00:12:26,210
So here's why the stock market crashed.

262
00:12:26,230 --> 00:12:30,142
A market that's one-third AI had been sliding for a month.

263
00:12:30,162 --> 00:12:35,466
Then, in three days, voters elected a Congress that might rein in data centers,

264
00:12:35,486 --> 00:12:38,698
Beijing left six hundred thousand chips at the door,

265
00:12:38,718 --> 00:12:41,710
and funds sitting on a great year cashed out.

266
00:12:41,730 --> 00:12:42,702
Nothing broke.

267
00:12:42,722 --> 00:12:43,818
The fear did it.

268
00:12:43,838 --> 00:12:45,390
It isn't new, either.

269
00:12:45,410 --> 00:12:49,142
In the eighteen-forties, Britain went mad for railways,

270
00:12:49,162 --> 00:12:53,654
and at the peak it was pouring about seven percent of its economy into track.

271
00:12:53,674 --> 00:12:56,946
Railway shares lost nearly two thirds of their value,

272
00:12:56,966 --> 00:13:0,298
and a third or more of the approved lines never got built.

273
00:13:0,318 --> 00:13:4,759
But many of the lines that did get built are still part of Britain's railway today.

274
00:13:4,779 --> 00:13:5,951
Here's the catch.

275
00:13:5,971 --> 00:13:8,363
A railway can wait for its trains.

276
00:13:8,383 --> 00:13:11,456
A chip sitting in a dark building just gets older.

277
00:13:11,476 --> 00:13:14,691
So, was Thursday the AI bubble popping?

278
00:13:14,711 --> 00:13:15,703
Not yet.

279
00:13:15,723 --> 00:13:19,575
Both tariff-crash days in April twenty twenty-five were bigger,

280
00:13:19,595 --> 00:13:23,987
and together erased a record six point six trillion dollars.

281
00:13:24,007 --> 00:13:27,879
Jobless claims were near their lowest since nineteen sixty-nine.

282
00:13:27,899 --> 00:13:29,771
And no rule had passed.

283
00:13:29,791 --> 00:13:33,954
Bernie Sanders called for a national moratorium on data centers.

284
00:13:33,974 --> 00:13:37,993
Americans don't want Big Tech oligarchs wrecking the environment...

285
00:13:38,013 --> 00:13:39,887
A call, not a bill.

286
00:13:39,907 --> 00:13:42,599
A bubble doesn't pop when prices fall.

287
00:13:42,619 --> 00:13:44,591
It pops when the money stops.

288
00:13:44,611 --> 00:13:47,303
On Thursday, the money hadn't stopped.

289
00:13:47,323 --> 00:13:49,575
Nvidia's sales were still doubling.

290
00:13:49,595 --> 00:13:53,949
The giants were still expected to spend more than a trillion dollars next year.

291
00:13:53,969 --> 00:13:56,741
But here's the part almost nobody noticed.

292
00:13:56,761 --> 00:14:0,105
A week before the crash, one giant blinked.

293
00:14:0,125 --> 00:14:2,265
Microsoft cut its spending plan from a

294
00:14:2,285 --> 00:14:4,865
hundred and seventy-five billion dollars to a

295
00:14:4,885 --> 00:14:6,037
hundred and seventy.

296
00:14:6,057 --> 00:14:7,949
That's less than three percent.

297
00:14:7,969 --> 00:14:8,601
Tiny.

298
00:14:8,621 --> 00:14:11,133
But it's a foot moving toward the brake.

299
00:14:11,153 --> 00:14:12,253
And on Tuesday,

300
00:14:12,273 --> 00:14:13,933
the people who pay the electric bill

301
00:14:13,953 --> 00:14:16,413
elected a Congress that might want a say in

302
00:14:16,433 --> 00:14:17,627
where the buildings go.

303
00:14:17,647 --> 00:14:19,679
So Thursday wasn't the pop.

304
00:14:19,699 --> 00:14:23,451
It was the day the market noticed there's a pin, and that voters,

305
00:14:23,471 --> 00:14:26,681
Washington and Beijing all have a hand on it.

306
00:14:26,701 --> 00:14:30,413
Nvidia is now about a quarter below its October record.

307
00:14:30,433 --> 00:14:33,425
Its next report is due on the seventeenth of November,

308
00:14:33,445 --> 00:14:36,777
and the six hundred thousand chips are still in Hong Kong.

309
00:14:36,797 --> 00:14:39,209
The rally died in six minutes.

310
00:14:39,229 --> 00:14:44,533
What happens next gets decided much more slowly, by permits, power lines,

311
00:14:44,553 --> 00:14:47,537
and an electric bill on a kitchen table in Ohio.

312
00:14:47,557 --> 00:14:52,449
On Thursday, Lisa Su said the market can be a little bit short-sighted.

313
00:14:52,469 --> 00:14:57,479
That afternoon, it might have been the furthest it had looked in months.

How a Google engineer with three jobs copied more than a thousand files on Google's AI chips, and what he got for it.

Linwei "Leon" Ding joined Google in 2019 and worked on the software that runs its AI supercomputers. From May 2022 he took screenshots of Google's chip documents, pasted them into a notes app, saved them as PDFs and uploaded them to his own account, while he was the technology chief of a startup in Beijing and then the boss of his own AI company in Shanghai. Google found out after he pitched investors on a stage in Beijing. A jury convicted him on fourteen counts in January 2026, a judge threw out the seven espionage counts in August, and he was sentenced to twelve months minus a day.

1
00:00:0,156 --> 00:00:1,153
This is Leon.

2
00:00:1,173 --> 00:00:3,357
And Leon has three jobs.

3
00:00:3,377 --> 00:00:8,248
Job one: he's an engineer at Google, on the supercomputers that train its AI.

4
00:00:8,268 --> 00:00:12,307
Job two: he's the technology chief of an AI startup in Beijing.

5
00:00:12,327 --> 00:00:16,176
Job three: he's the boss of his own AI company in Shanghai.

6
00:00:16,196 --> 00:00:18,308
Google only knows about the first one.

7
00:00:18,328 --> 00:00:19,452
Where are you going?

8
00:00:19,472 --> 00:00:20,192
Lunch.

9
00:00:20,212 --> 00:00:21,212
For how long?

10
00:00:21,232 --> 00:00:22,223
Keep swiping.

11
00:00:22,243 --> 00:00:23,183
For a year,

12
00:00:23,203 --> 00:00:27,783
Leon carried Google's most secret chip designs out of job one and into the other

13
00:00:27,803 --> 00:00:28,140
two.

14
00:00:28,160 --> 00:00:29,960
More than a thousand files.

15
00:00:29,980 --> 00:00:31,191
And he didn't need a rope.

16
00:00:31,211 --> 00:00:32,470
He used the Notes app.

17
00:00:32,490 --> 00:00:35,142
So why did Google hire a Chinese spy?

18
00:00:35,162 --> 00:00:38,492
And how did he rob it with copy and paste?

19
00:00:44,879 --> 00:00:49,411
For ten years, Google built a chip and wouldn't sell it to anyone.

20
00:00:49,431 --> 00:00:50,715
Not for sale.

21
00:00:50,735 --> 00:00:52,103
Not even for...

22
00:00:52,123 --> 00:00:53,227
Not for sale.

23
00:00:53,247 --> 00:00:55,951
It starts in twenty thirteen, with a sum.

24
00:00:55,971 --> 00:01:0,671
Google's engineers work out what happens if everyone talks to their phone for just

25
00:01:0,691 --> 00:01:1,975
three minutes a day.

26
00:01:1,995 --> 00:01:3,687
Three minutes a day, each.

27
00:01:3,707 --> 00:01:4,987
That's nothing.

28
00:01:5,007 --> 00:01:7,440
That's twice as many data centers.

29
00:01:7,460 --> 00:01:9,332
So you build more buildings?

30
00:01:9,352 --> 00:01:11,113
We build a better chip.

31
00:01:11,133 --> 00:01:14,016
Don't the chips we have already do everything?

32
00:01:14,036 --> 00:01:15,216
That's the problem.

33
00:01:15,236 --> 00:01:16,858
We need one that does one thing.

34
00:01:16,878 --> 00:01:20,542
They call it the Tensor Processing Unit, the TPU,

35
00:01:20,562 --> 00:01:23,234
and they have it working in fifteen months.

36
00:01:23,254 --> 00:01:26,686
A normal AI chip is a kitchen that can cook anything.

37
00:01:26,706 --> 00:01:28,870
Google's chip is a pizza oven.

38
00:01:28,890 --> 00:01:33,274
It makes one thing, the math AI runs on, and it makes it fast.

39
00:01:33,294 --> 00:01:36,926
That chip helped AlphaGo beat the world champion at Go.

40
00:01:36,946 --> 00:01:39,318
Today Google's Gemini is trained on it.

41
00:01:39,338 --> 00:01:41,470
And that makes Google strange,

42
00:01:41,490 --> 00:01:45,516
because almost everyone else in AI has to stand in one line.

43
00:01:45,536 --> 00:01:46,333
Next!

44
00:01:46,353 --> 00:01:47,633
Where's Google?

45
00:01:47,653 --> 00:01:48,900
Making their own.

46
00:01:48,920 --> 00:01:51,098
Can I skip the line?

47
00:01:51,259 --> 00:01:52,894
Nobody skips the line.

48
00:01:52,914 --> 00:01:57,806
When Google's chips had their big moment in November twenty twenty-five, Nvidia,

49
00:01:57,826 --> 00:02:0,158
which almost never talks about a rival,

50
00:02:0,178 --> 00:02:3,909
posted one line: "We're delighted by Google's success."

51
00:02:3,929 --> 00:02:4,641
Okay.

52
00:02:4,661 --> 00:02:5,875
Can I rent it?

53
00:02:5,895 --> 00:02:7,295
Now we're talking.

54
00:02:7,315 --> 00:02:9,307
Then the rest of the world wanted in.

55
00:02:9,327 --> 00:02:12,419
Anthropic signed up for as many as a million of them,

56
00:02:12,439 --> 00:02:15,511
and the bill runs into the tens of billions.

57
00:02:15,531 --> 00:02:21,043
Bloomberg's analysts expect TPU sales to grow more than ten times in two years,

58
00:02:21,063 --> 00:02:24,235
to over a hundred and thirty-five billion dollars.

59
00:02:24,255 --> 00:02:26,539
For a chip you can only rent.

60
00:02:26,559 --> 00:02:31,739
One firm put the chips and Google's AI lab together at about nine hundred billion

61
00:02:31,759 --> 00:02:32,531
dollars.

62
00:02:32,551 --> 00:02:36,889
That's about two and a half thousand dollars for every person in America.

63
00:02:36,909 --> 00:02:41,633
And the recipe for all of it is written down: how the chip is laid out inside,

64
00:02:41,653 --> 00:02:44,925
the software that makes thousands of them work as one machine,

65
00:02:44,945 --> 00:02:47,137
the network card that wires them together.

66
00:02:47,157 --> 00:02:49,209
It all sits in documents.

67
00:02:49,229 --> 00:02:53,759
And in twenty nineteen, Google gave a new hire the key.

68
00:02:55,017 --> 00:02:57,269
May thirteenth, twenty nineteen.

69
00:02:57,289 --> 00:02:59,323
Leon's first day at Google.

70
00:02:59,343 --> 00:03:2,795
He came to America in twenty ten for a master's degree.

71
00:03:2,815 --> 00:03:4,931
Quiet, polite, mid-level.

72
00:03:4,951 --> 00:03:6,523
He doesn't design the chips.

73
00:03:6,543 --> 00:03:11,535
His job is the software that keeps them busy inside Google's AI supercomputers.

74
00:03:11,555 --> 00:03:14,855
But you can't keep a chip busy if you don't know how it works,

75
00:03:14,875 --> 00:03:17,083
so he's cleared to read the blueprints.

76
00:03:17,103 --> 00:03:19,075
So that's why Google hired him.

77
00:03:19,095 --> 00:03:20,667
It didn't hire a spy.

78
00:03:20,687 --> 00:03:24,059
It hired a good engineer, and it gave him the keys,

79
00:03:24,079 --> 00:03:26,226
because the job can't be done without them.

80
00:03:26,246 --> 00:03:29,050
For three years, nothing happens.

81
00:03:29,070 --> 00:03:32,222
Then, on May twenty-first, twenty twenty-two,

82
00:03:32,242 --> 00:03:36,421
Leon makes his first upload of Google's files to his own account.

83
00:03:36,441 --> 00:03:38,175
Just backing up my notes.

84
00:03:38,195 --> 00:03:41,867
Twenty-three days later, an email arrives from Beijing.

85
00:03:41,887 --> 00:03:45,615
It's from Yuan Ye, the boss of a startup called Rongshu.

86
00:03:45,635 --> 00:03:47,295
Chief technology officer.

87
00:03:47,315 --> 00:03:48,947
A hundred thousand yuan a month.

88
00:03:48,967 --> 00:03:49,987
Plus a bonus.

89
00:03:50,007 --> 00:03:50,951
Plus stock.

90
00:03:50,971 --> 00:03:53,054
That's very generous.

91
00:03:53,074 --> 00:03:55,133
So when do you quit Google?

92
00:03:55,153 --> 00:03:56,876
Why would I quit Google?

93
00:03:56,896 --> 00:03:59,223
How much is a hundred thousand yuan?

94
00:03:59,243 --> 00:04:1,448
About fourteen thousand eight hundred dollars.

95
00:04:1,468 --> 00:04:2,218
A year?

96
00:04:2,238 --> 00:04:2,974
A month.

97
00:04:2,994 --> 00:04:6,358
That's a decent used car, every single month.

98
00:04:6,378 --> 00:04:9,445
About a hundred and seventy-seven thousand dollars a year.

99
00:04:9,465 --> 00:04:12,417
He says yes, and he keeps the Google badge.

100
00:04:12,437 --> 00:04:16,509
Now Leon is a spy inside Google for a Chinese company,

101
00:04:16,529 --> 00:04:18,506
and Google is still paying him.

102
00:04:18,526 --> 00:04:19,589
Two jobs?

103
00:04:19,609 --> 00:04:20,447
Two badges.

104
00:04:20,467 --> 00:04:22,079
And which one does he need?

105
00:04:22,099 --> 00:04:23,425
The one that opens the vault.

106
00:04:23,445 --> 00:04:26,397
But the second job needs something from the first.

107
00:04:26,417 --> 00:04:30,147
And Google has an alarm for exactly that.

108
00:04:31,519 --> 00:04:34,571
So how do you get a secret file out of Google?

109
00:04:34,591 --> 00:04:35,311
You don't.

110
00:04:35,331 --> 00:04:38,803
Google logs every file that leaves for a cloud drive.

111
00:04:38,823 --> 00:04:41,643
Send one of its secret documents to your own account,

112
00:04:41,663 --> 00:04:43,920
and the alarm goes off at once.

113
00:04:43,940 --> 00:04:45,847
If I send the file...

114
00:04:45,867 --> 00:04:46,842
We see it.

115
00:04:46,862 --> 00:04:49,182
And if I never send a file?

116
00:04:49,202 --> 00:04:50,538
Then there's nothing to see.

117
00:04:50,558 --> 00:04:52,796
So Leon never sends a file.

118
00:04:52,816 --> 00:04:56,294
Step one, he takes a screenshot of a Google document.

119
00:04:56,314 --> 00:05:0,878
Step two, he pastes it into Apple Notes, on the MacBook Google gave him.

120
00:05:0,898 --> 00:05:4,022
Step three, he saves the note as a PDF.

121
00:05:4,042 --> 00:05:8,037
Step four, he uploads that PDF to his own Google account.

122
00:05:8,057 --> 00:05:10,981
To the alarm, that isn't a stolen file.

123
00:05:11,001 --> 00:05:13,167
It's a man backing up his own notes.

124
00:05:13,187 --> 00:05:14,815
Is that a shopping list?

125
00:05:14,835 --> 00:05:15,980
It is now.

126
00:05:16,000 --> 00:05:18,547
He robbed Google with the Notes app?

127
00:05:18,567 --> 00:05:19,806
And a PDF.

128
00:05:19,826 --> 00:05:21,711
So where does he keep it all?

129
00:05:21,731 --> 00:05:22,554
In the cloud.

130
00:05:22,574 --> 00:05:23,642
Whose cloud?

131
00:05:23,662 --> 00:05:24,397
Google's.

132
00:05:24,417 --> 00:05:27,629
The stolen files sit on Google's own servers,

133
00:05:27,649 --> 00:05:30,635
kept safe for him by the company he's stealing from.

134
00:05:30,655 --> 00:05:32,427
He keeps it up for a year.

135
00:05:32,447 --> 00:05:35,319
Screenshot, paste, save, upload.

136
00:05:35,339 --> 00:05:40,173
By the end, it's more than a thousand files, over two thousand pages.

137
00:05:40,193 --> 00:05:45,773
And what's on them is the recipe behind a business one firm valued at nine hundred

138
00:05:45,793 --> 00:05:47,355
billion dollars.

139
00:05:47,375 --> 00:05:49,629
So what's actually in here?

140
00:05:49,649 --> 00:05:52,619
How the TPU is built inside, part by part.

141
00:05:52,639 --> 00:05:53,490
And?

142
00:05:53,510 --> 00:05:57,156
The software that runs thousands of them as one giant computer.

143
00:05:57,176 --> 00:05:57,957
And?

144
00:05:57,977 --> 00:06:2,121
The secret chip in Google's network card, so they can all talk to each other.

145
00:06:2,141 --> 00:06:4,677
So, the cake recipe.

146
00:06:4,697 --> 00:06:8,505
The recipe, the oven, and the plans for the whole bakery.

147
00:06:8,525 --> 00:06:11,469
No rope, no mask, no lasers.

148
00:06:11,489 --> 00:06:14,021
Nobody carries the vault out of Google.

149
00:06:14,041 --> 00:06:16,713
Leon photographs it, one page at a time,

150
00:06:16,733 --> 00:06:19,175
and keeps the pages under his shopping list.

151
00:06:19,195 --> 00:06:20,290
Anything leaving?

152
00:06:20,310 --> 00:06:21,219
Just notes.

153
00:06:21,239 --> 00:06:23,191
So now he has the pages.

154
00:06:23,211 --> 00:06:28,381
What he doesn't have is the faintest idea how to build what's on them.

155
00:06:29,703 --> 00:06:34,992
In October twenty twenty-two, a Google engineer goes to China for five months.

156
00:06:35,012 --> 00:06:39,096
From December, Leon is sitting in Rongshu's meetings with investors.

157
00:06:39,116 --> 00:06:44,640
Early the next year, he and Yuan Ye start a new company together, Shanghai Zhisuan.

158
00:06:44,660 --> 00:06:47,484
By May, Leon is its chief executive.

159
00:06:47,504 --> 00:06:48,716
That's job three.

160
00:06:48,736 --> 00:06:52,958
The plan is simple: take Google's playbook and sell it in China.

161
00:06:52,978 --> 00:06:54,061
Google built it.

162
00:06:54,081 --> 00:06:55,287
I've read it.

163
00:06:55,307 --> 00:06:56,760
Then we build it.

164
00:06:56,780 --> 00:06:58,127
I have notes.

165
00:06:58,147 --> 00:07:2,739
The fundraisers helping them believe Leon has already built the technology.

166
00:07:2,759 --> 00:07:3,663
He hasn't.

167
00:07:3,683 --> 00:07:5,661
You built this yourself?

168
00:07:5,681 --> 00:07:7,226
I know it very well.

169
00:07:7,246 --> 00:07:9,106
How many chips has it run on?

170
00:07:9,126 --> 00:07:10,294
Ten thousand.

171
00:07:10,314 --> 00:07:11,695
Your chips?

172
00:07:11,715 --> 00:07:12,900
Give me a moment.

173
00:07:12,920 --> 00:07:17,194
In April twenty twenty-three, the investors want more detail.

174
00:07:17,214 --> 00:07:21,502
How exactly does your software hand out work to ten thousand chips?

175
00:07:21,522 --> 00:07:22,462
Great question.

176
00:07:22,482 --> 00:07:23,637
Let me check my notes.

177
00:07:23,657 --> 00:07:25,489
So Leon steals more.

178
00:07:25,509 --> 00:07:29,727
In the judge's words, he "hurriedly uploaded more documents."

179
00:07:29,747 --> 00:07:32,879
He's stealing to answer his own investors' questions.

180
00:07:32,899 --> 00:07:35,791
His last big batch goes up on April seventeenth.

181
00:07:35,811 --> 00:07:37,643
That same day in Beijing,

182
00:07:37,663 --> 00:07:41,726
Yuan Ye tells investors Leon is Rongshu's technology chief.

183
00:07:41,746 --> 00:07:44,990
To prove the tech is his, Leon films a demo.

184
00:07:45,010 --> 00:07:48,292
It shows him running a test on Google's own chips.

185
00:07:48,312 --> 00:07:49,524
Impressive.

186
00:07:49,544 --> 00:07:50,601
Where's it running?

187
00:07:50,621 --> 00:07:51,396
The cloud.

188
00:07:51,416 --> 00:07:52,493
Whose cloud?

189
00:07:52,513 --> 00:07:53,452
Next question.

190
00:07:53,472 --> 00:07:56,904
His company later wrote its strategy down for its own team.

191
00:07:56,924 --> 00:08:1,436
Quote: "We have experience with Google's ten-thousand-card computational power

192
00:08:1,456 --> 00:08:4,464
platform; we just need to replicate and upgrade it."

193
00:08:4,484 --> 00:08:5,607
Replicate.

194
00:08:5,627 --> 00:08:6,948
And upgrade.

195
00:08:6,968 --> 00:08:8,200
And it works.

196
00:08:8,220 --> 00:08:11,872
One of China's best-known startup schools, MiraclePlus,

197
00:08:11,892 --> 00:08:16,024
puts in about seven hundred thousand dollars for seven percent of the company.

198
00:08:16,044 --> 00:08:19,210
That's about four years of Leon's Rongshu salary.

199
00:08:19,230 --> 00:08:20,302
Seven percent.

200
00:08:20,322 --> 00:08:22,424
For a company with no product.

201
00:08:22,444 --> 00:08:23,119
Yet.

202
00:08:23,139 --> 00:08:24,545
And when do we see it?

203
00:08:24,565 --> 00:08:25,224
Soon.

204
00:08:25,244 --> 00:08:28,696
That makes Zhisuan worth about ten million dollars.

205
00:08:28,716 --> 00:08:31,628
Google spends that in about twenty-six minutes.

206
00:08:31,648 --> 00:08:35,267
That's about three hundred and ninety thousand dollars a minute.

207
00:08:35,287 --> 00:08:36,947
Ten million dollars?

208
00:08:36,967 --> 00:08:37,842
For what?

209
00:08:37,862 --> 00:08:38,985
A copy of Google.

210
00:08:39,005 --> 00:08:40,377
Has he made the copy?

211
00:08:40,397 --> 00:08:41,554
He's made the PDF.

212
00:08:41,574 --> 00:08:43,246
There's just one problem.

213
00:08:43,266 --> 00:08:46,438
The boss of a Shanghai startup has to be in China.

214
00:08:46,458 --> 00:08:49,030
A Google engineer has to be in California.

215
00:08:49,050 --> 00:08:51,767
And Google's doors keep score.

216
00:08:51,768 --> 00:08:53,940
Three jobs and a notes app.

217
00:08:53,960 --> 00:08:55,736
I can't even get a second one.

218
00:08:55,756 --> 00:08:56,986
Try a legal one.

219
00:08:57,006 --> 00:08:58,278
Funny you say that.

220
00:08:58,298 --> 00:09:0,764
You've been watching one for nine minutes.

221
00:09:0,784 --> 00:09:1,949
The cartoon?

222
00:09:1,969 --> 00:09:2,941
This video.

223
00:09:2,961 --> 00:09:5,793
The script, the voices, the lasers.

224
00:09:5,813 --> 00:09:10,897
Every shot and every sound effect, from a topic to a finished four K film,

225
00:09:10,917 --> 00:09:11,557
overnight.

226
00:09:11,577 --> 00:09:15,509
We make every video on this channel with a studio called Overnight.

227
00:09:15,529 --> 00:09:18,231
And they've just opened the app they use to the public.

228
00:09:18,251 --> 00:09:19,603
You give it an idea.

229
00:09:19,623 --> 00:09:23,275
Your own Claude researches it, writes it, voices it,

230
00:09:23,295 --> 00:09:27,763
builds every shot and mixes the sound, on your own Mac or PC.

231
00:09:27,783 --> 00:09:29,615
So I could make this.

232
00:09:29,635 --> 00:09:30,587
Myself.

233
00:09:30,607 --> 00:09:31,986
At this quality.

234
00:09:32,006 --> 00:09:32,757
Yes.

235
00:09:32,777 --> 00:09:33,782
With the charts?

236
00:09:33,802 --> 00:09:34,584
Yes.

237
00:09:34,604 --> 00:09:35,745
And the lasers?

238
00:09:35,765 --> 00:09:37,177
And the lasers.

239
00:09:37,197 --> 00:09:39,609
There are more than twenty-five styles in it.

240
00:09:39,629 --> 00:09:41,221
Money stories like this one.

241
00:09:41,241 --> 00:09:43,113
Three D news documentaries.

242
00:09:43,133 --> 00:09:44,725
Three D cartoon Shorts.

243
00:09:44,745 --> 00:09:46,012
Minecraft Shorts.

244
00:09:46,032 --> 00:09:50,722
It was a hundred forty-seven dollars a month, and right now it's eighty-seven.

245
00:09:50,742 --> 00:09:53,474
But the price is going up as more people join.

246
00:09:53,494 --> 00:09:55,577
Whatever you join at stays yours.

247
00:09:55,597 --> 00:10:0,089
And at three hundred members, Overnight closes the doors to the public again.

248
00:10:0,109 --> 00:10:3,046
Nobody wants the internet flooded with these.

249
00:10:3,066 --> 00:10:4,018
Three hundred.

250
00:10:4,038 --> 00:10:4,605
Got it.

251
00:10:4,625 --> 00:10:7,637
Make fourteen videos in your first thirty days.

252
00:10:7,657 --> 00:10:10,601
If you're not happy with them, you get your first month back.

253
00:10:10,621 --> 00:10:12,393
made overnight dot com.

254
00:10:12,413 --> 00:10:15,451
It's on screen, and it's the first link in the description.

255
00:10:15,471 --> 00:10:18,035
Now, back to the man with three jobs.

256
00:10:18,055 --> 00:10:20,327
He can't be in two countries at once.

257
00:10:20,347 --> 00:10:23,917
And Google's doors are about to notice.

258
00:10:25,550 --> 00:10:29,734
Google has a second alarm, and it has the best name in security.

259
00:10:29,754 --> 00:10:32,646
It's called the Impossible Location Signal.

260
00:10:32,666 --> 00:10:34,273
Impossible Location?

261
00:10:34,293 --> 00:10:36,193
Your laptop logs in from Beijing.

262
00:10:36,213 --> 00:10:38,226
Your badge says you're in California.

263
00:10:38,246 --> 00:10:39,524
Can't be both.

264
00:10:39,544 --> 00:10:41,120
So the alarm fires.

265
00:10:41,140 --> 00:10:42,577
So how do you beat it?

266
00:10:42,597 --> 00:10:44,269
You lend someone your badge.

267
00:10:44,289 --> 00:10:47,353
November twenty-fourth, twenty twenty-three.

268
00:10:47,373 --> 00:10:52,017
Leon walks onto a stage in Beijing, at MiraclePlus's big investor day,

269
00:10:52,037 --> 00:10:54,649
as the chief executive of Zhisuan, a

270
00:10:54,669 --> 00:10:57,561
ten-million-dollar company with no product.

271
00:10:57,581 --> 00:11:3,533
His slide says "government agencies" and "supercomputing centers" "will be our

272
00:11:3,553 --> 00:11:3,853
customers."

273
00:11:3,873 --> 00:11:5,660
Chief executive now.

274
00:11:5,680 --> 00:11:7,359
And Google engineer.

275
00:11:7,379 --> 00:11:8,420
Not tonight.

276
00:11:8,440 --> 00:11:9,842
And your background?

277
00:11:9,862 --> 00:11:10,951
Google.

278
00:11:10,971 --> 00:11:12,557
Does Google know you're here?

279
00:11:12,577 --> 00:11:13,372
Next slide.

280
00:11:13,392 --> 00:11:16,664
Back in California, his badge keeps going to work.

281
00:11:16,684 --> 00:11:19,064
His intern swipes it into his Google office

282
00:11:19,084 --> 00:11:21,776
on December fourth, sixth and eighth.

283
00:11:21,796 --> 00:11:23,973
Monday, Wednesday, Friday.

284
00:11:23,993 --> 00:11:25,325
It's Wednesday.

285
00:11:25,345 --> 00:11:26,302
I swiped.

286
00:11:26,322 --> 00:11:26,974
Good.

287
00:11:26,994 --> 00:11:28,015
Friday too.

288
00:11:28,035 --> 00:11:30,177
Do I have to do your smile?

289
00:11:30,197 --> 00:11:31,380
Just swipe.

290
00:11:31,400 --> 00:11:33,223
And if someone asks where you are?

291
00:11:33,243 --> 00:11:34,067
Traveling.

292
00:11:34,087 --> 00:11:36,259
But the badge can't cover everything.

293
00:11:36,279 --> 00:11:40,455
Two days before the first swipe, on December second, from China,

294
00:11:40,475 --> 00:11:43,867
Leon uploads more files to a second personal account.

295
00:11:43,887 --> 00:11:46,383
And this time, Google notices.

296
00:11:46,403 --> 00:11:47,567
A second account.

297
00:11:47,587 --> 00:11:49,177
Full of our files.

298
00:11:49,197 --> 00:11:49,915
Leon.

299
00:11:49,935 --> 00:11:51,327
On December eighth,

300
00:11:51,347 --> 00:11:57,637
the investigator who never saw a thing finally asks Leon a simple question.

301
00:11:59,049 --> 00:12:1,459
Why are our files in your account?

302
00:12:1,479 --> 00:12:3,193
Evidence of my work.

303
00:12:3,213 --> 00:12:5,048
These are our chip designs.

304
00:12:5,068 --> 00:12:6,474
Which I work on.

305
00:12:6,494 --> 00:12:8,579
And are you planning to leave?

306
00:12:8,599 --> 00:12:9,247
No.

307
00:12:9,267 --> 00:12:12,047
He tells Google he has "no intention of

308
00:12:12,067 --> 00:12:15,179
leaving Google." Then he signs a sworn paper

309
00:12:15,199 --> 00:12:17,471
saying he has deleted every file.

310
00:12:17,491 --> 00:12:20,047
It's called a self-deletion affidavit.

311
00:12:20,067 --> 00:12:21,292
Everything's gone?

312
00:12:21,312 --> 00:12:22,065
Everything.

313
00:12:22,085 --> 00:12:24,897
Six days later, on December fourteenth,

314
00:12:24,917 --> 00:12:28,509
Leon downloads every stolen file to his computer at home.

315
00:12:28,529 --> 00:12:33,001
The same day, he books a one-way ticket from San Francisco to Beijing,

316
00:12:33,021 --> 00:12:34,260
for January seventh.

317
00:12:34,280 --> 00:12:35,432
Six days.

318
00:12:35,452 --> 00:12:38,406
A carton of milk lasts longer than that promise.

319
00:12:38,426 --> 00:12:41,458
On December twenty-sixth, he quits by email.

320
00:12:41,478 --> 00:12:43,864
His last day will be January fifth.

321
00:12:43,884 --> 00:12:44,676
Hang on.

322
00:12:44,696 --> 00:12:47,469
Didn't he say he had no intention of leaving?

323
00:12:47,489 --> 00:12:48,180
Yes.

324
00:12:48,200 --> 00:12:48,919
When?

325
00:12:48,939 --> 00:12:50,107
Eighteen days ago.

326
00:12:50,127 --> 00:12:54,071
Then, on December twenty-ninth, Google finds the keynote.

327
00:12:54,091 --> 00:12:58,708
The chief executive of a startup in Beijing is one of its own engineers.

328
00:12:58,728 --> 00:13:0,235
That's Leon.

329
00:13:0,255 --> 00:13:0,965
Lock it.

330
00:13:0,985 --> 00:13:4,757
Google cuts off his access and locks his laptop from afar.

331
00:13:4,777 --> 00:13:9,029
It goes back through his history and finds nineteen months of uploads.

332
00:13:9,049 --> 00:13:13,304
Then it checks the door cameras, and someone else is holding his badge.

333
00:13:13,324 --> 00:13:16,205
If Leon was on a stage in Beijing...

334
00:13:16,225 --> 00:13:18,234
who's been going to work for him?

335
00:13:18,254 --> 00:13:19,026
Cut off,

336
00:13:19,046 --> 00:13:23,519
Leon rushes into the office at seven in the morning to get back on the network.

337
00:13:23,539 --> 00:13:24,319
Come on.

338
00:13:24,339 --> 00:13:25,259
Come on.

339
00:13:25,279 --> 00:13:26,191
Okay.

340
00:13:26,211 --> 00:13:27,048
Plan B.

341
00:13:27,068 --> 00:13:28,486
It doesn't work.

342
00:13:28,506 --> 00:13:31,099
So he deletes the files on his laptop.

343
00:13:31,119 --> 00:13:32,699
He deleted the files?

344
00:13:32,719 --> 00:13:33,611
From the laptop.

345
00:13:33,631 --> 00:13:35,344
And the copies in his cloud?

346
00:13:35,364 --> 00:13:36,416
Forgot those.

347
00:13:36,436 --> 00:13:38,048
Still on Google's servers.

348
00:13:38,068 --> 00:13:38,897
Still full.

349
00:13:38,917 --> 00:13:40,389
On January fourth,

350
00:13:40,409 --> 00:13:44,221
Google's security team collects his laptop and phone from his home.

351
00:13:44,241 --> 00:13:49,272
On January sixth, one day before the flight, the FBI is at his door.

352
00:13:49,292 --> 00:13:50,321
Going somewhere?

353
00:13:50,341 --> 00:13:51,186
Tomorrow.

354
00:13:51,206 --> 00:13:52,214
Not anymore.

355
00:13:52,234 --> 00:13:55,238
A week later, agents open his cloud accounts.

356
00:13:55,258 --> 00:14:0,290
More than a thousand files, sitting on Google's own servers the whole time.

357
00:14:0,310 --> 00:14:2,534
Caught, with the note in his hand.

358
00:14:2,554 --> 00:14:6,764
Now America had to decide what Leon was.

359
00:14:8,092 --> 00:14:10,264
March sixth, twenty twenty-four.

360
00:14:10,284 --> 00:14:14,305
The Attorney General of the United States announces one arrest.

361
00:14:14,325 --> 00:14:18,625
The Justice Department will not tolerate the theft of artificial intelligence and

362
00:14:18,645 --> 00:14:22,707
other advanced technologies that could put our national security at risk.

363
00:14:22,727 --> 00:14:27,351
In January twenty twenty-six, Leon goes on trial in San Francisco.

364
00:14:27,371 --> 00:14:28,663
Eleven days.

365
00:14:28,683 --> 00:14:30,815
Our note is now Exhibit A.

366
00:14:30,835 --> 00:14:33,888
His lawyer's best line went after the victim.

367
00:14:33,908 --> 00:14:36,478
Google chose openness over security.

368
00:14:36,498 --> 00:14:37,961
Is that a defense?

369
00:14:37,981 --> 00:14:39,463
It's a complaint about the lock.

370
00:14:39,483 --> 00:14:44,355
Google's security team takes the stand and walks the jury through the trick: notes

371
00:14:44,375 --> 00:14:48,982
turned into PDFs, so every upload looked like his own new file.

372
00:14:49,002 --> 00:14:51,846
To our alarms, it looked like notes.

373
00:14:51,866 --> 00:14:53,231
It was our chips.

374
00:14:53,251 --> 00:14:54,938
Then the jury goes out.

375
00:14:54,958 --> 00:14:56,353
They're back already?

376
00:14:56,373 --> 00:14:57,645
About three hours.

377
00:14:57,665 --> 00:14:59,181
For fourteen counts?

378
00:14:59,201 --> 00:15:1,125
About thirteen minutes a count.

379
00:15:1,145 --> 00:15:3,837
Guilty on all fourteen counts.

380
00:15:3,857 --> 00:15:8,129
Seven for stealing trade secrets, and seven for economic espionage.

381
00:15:8,149 --> 00:15:10,049
The government calls it the first-ever

382
00:15:10,069 --> 00:15:13,249
conviction on AI-related economic espionage

383
00:15:13,269 --> 00:15:13,958
charges.

384
00:15:13,978 --> 00:15:14,918
On paper,

385
00:15:14,938 --> 00:15:19,318
those counts add up to a hundred and seventy-five years in prison and nearly

386
00:15:19,338 --> 00:15:22,210
thirty-seven million dollars in fines.

387
00:15:22,230 --> 00:15:24,102
So when would he get out?

388
00:15:24,122 --> 00:15:25,606
Around the year twenty-two hundred.

389
00:15:25,626 --> 00:15:26,991
And the fines?

390
00:15:27,011 --> 00:15:29,220
About two hundred years of his Rongshu pay.

391
00:15:29,240 --> 00:15:33,709
But in August, the judge throws out all seven espionage counts.

392
00:15:33,729 --> 00:15:34,909
For spying,

393
00:15:34,929 --> 00:15:39,261
the law needs him to mean to help China's government at the moment he stole.

394
00:15:39,281 --> 00:15:43,519
And the stealing came months before he ever pitched anyone in government.

395
00:15:43,539 --> 00:15:45,587
So who was he spying for?

396
00:15:45,607 --> 00:15:46,446
Not Beijing.

397
00:15:46,466 --> 00:15:47,435
Then who?

398
00:15:47,455 --> 00:15:48,094
Leon.

399
00:15:48,114 --> 00:15:51,814
Ding had no product; he was just pretending he had one.

400
00:15:51,834 --> 00:15:56,078
The judge called the plot to help China "ad hoc, disorganized,

401
00:15:56,098 --> 00:15:59,000
and feeble." The theft was another matter.

402
00:15:59,020 --> 00:16:3,466
This was a systematic, brazen effort to steal Google's property.

403
00:16:3,486 --> 00:16:8,638
On September first, twenty twenty-six, he sentences Leon to twelve months,

404
00:16:8,658 --> 00:16:9,744
minus one day.

405
00:16:9,764 --> 00:16:12,634
From a hundred and seventy-five years...

406
00:16:12,654 --> 00:16:14,710
To three hundred and sixty-four days.

407
00:16:14,730 --> 00:16:16,393
That's not even a year.

408
00:16:16,413 --> 00:16:17,425
By one day.

409
00:16:17,445 --> 00:16:21,985
That's still more than the Apple engineer who took self-driving car secrets to a

410
00:16:22,005 --> 00:16:23,157
Chinese car startup.

411
00:16:23,177 --> 00:16:24,563
He got four months.

412
00:16:24,583 --> 00:16:25,995
Then came the bill.

413
00:16:26,015 --> 00:16:30,767
In October, America put Zhisuan and MiraclePlus on a sanctions list.

414
00:16:30,787 --> 00:16:33,407
The startup school's seven-hundred-thousand-dollar

415
00:16:33,427 --> 00:16:35,759
bet now sits on a blacklist.

416
00:16:35,779 --> 00:16:40,269
Their money in America is frozen, and no American can invest in them.

417
00:16:40,289 --> 00:16:42,724
Seven percent of what, exactly?

418
00:16:42,744 --> 00:16:45,217
Replicate and upgrade?

419
00:16:45,237 --> 00:16:45,656
Frozen.

420
00:16:45,676 --> 00:16:49,418
And the case is back in court, on appeal.

421
00:16:50,663 --> 00:16:53,415
Leon started this story with three jobs.

422
00:16:53,435 --> 00:16:54,947
Now he has none.

423
00:16:54,967 --> 00:17:0,067
His own lawyers said he will "never again hold a position of trust at a technology

424
00:17:0,087 --> 00:17:0,682
company."

425
00:17:0,702 --> 00:17:2,528
Do you want this back?

426
00:17:2,548 --> 00:17:4,269
Nowhere left to swipe it.

427
00:17:4,289 --> 00:17:8,941
Google is spending about two hundred billion dollars this year to build AI.

428
00:17:8,961 --> 00:17:11,713
That's more than half a billion dollars a day.

429
00:17:11,733 --> 00:17:15,332
In the time it took to watch this, it spent about six million.

430
00:17:15,352 --> 00:17:20,250
And the lock on its most valuable recipe was beaten by a notes app, a PDF,

431
00:17:20,270 --> 00:17:21,958
and an intern with a badge.

432
00:17:21,978 --> 00:17:24,930
So why did Google hire a Chinese spy?

433
00:17:24,950 --> 00:17:25,722
It didn't.

434
00:17:25,742 --> 00:17:29,906
It hired an engineer, handed him the recipe, and trusted him with it.

435
00:17:29,926 --> 00:17:32,912
The spy showed up three years later, by email.

436
00:17:32,932 --> 00:17:36,814
The price for trying was three hundred and sixty-four days.

437
00:17:36,834 --> 00:17:40,257
And Leon got caught because he couldn't stay off a stage.

438
00:17:40,277 --> 00:17:44,487
So who's still sitting quietly at their desk tonight?

439
00:17:46,261 --> 00:17:46,893
Me.

440
00:17:46,913 --> 00:17:48,895
But I'm not copying anything.

441
00:17:48,915 --> 00:17:49,547
Good.

442
00:17:49,567 --> 00:17:50,319
Make your own.

443
00:17:50,339 --> 00:17:54,231
The app this video was made in is open to the public right now,

444
00:17:54,251 --> 00:17:56,361
at made overnight dot com.

445
00:17:56,381 --> 00:18:1,212
It was a hundred forty-seven dollars a month, and right now it's eighty-seven.

446
00:18:1,232 --> 00:18:3,884
But the price is going up as people join,

447
00:18:3,904 --> 00:18:6,496
and at three hundred members it closes again.

The link is first in the description.

6

7
00:00:18,416 --> 00:00:21,270

8
00:00:21,290 --> 00:00:25,249

9
00:00:25,269 --> 00:00:26,412
Was it blackmail?

00:00:26,432 --> 00:00:28,290

00:00:36,109 --> 00:00:38,621

00:00:38,641 --> 00:00:40,661
He sold them to a friend in Singapore,

18
00:00:40,681 --> 00:00:44,747
and every one of them left through the front door, in a box, with a receipt.

19
00:00:44,767 --> 00:00:46,427
So follow one box.

20
00:00:46,447 --> 00:00:52,337
At every stop, somebody gets paid, and the last name on the receipt is yours.

21
00:00:55,714 --> 00:01:1,486

22
00:01:1,506 --> 00:01:4,246
A year earlier, it went for a third of that.

23
00:01:4,266 --> 00:01:5,934
Nine hundred thousand.

24
00:01:5,954 --> 00:01:8,377
Last year it was three hundred!

25
00:01:8,397 --> 00:01:10,201
Then you should have bought it last year.

26
00:01:10,221 --> 00:01:14,213
That's a used car that triples in price while it sits in your driveway.

27
00:01:14,233 --> 00:01:15,825
What's inside that's worth it?

28
00:01:15,845 --> 00:01:19,149
Eight Nvidia chips, each the price of a new car.

29
00:01:19,169 --> 00:01:23,221
Each one does thousands of tiny sums at the very same moment,

30
00:01:23,241 --> 00:01:26,113
which is exactly what artificial intelligence needs.

31
00:01:26,133 --> 00:01:30,985
Wire tens of thousands of them together and you can train a model like ChatGPT.

32
00:01:31,005 --> 00:01:32,640
Eight of our best.

33
00:01:32,660 --> 00:01:33,924
What do they do?

34
00:01:33,944 --> 00:01:34,736
Math.

35
00:01:34,756 --> 00:01:35,408
All of it.

36
00:01:35,428 --> 00:01:36,277
At once.

37
00:01:36,297 --> 00:01:37,790
And who wants one?

38
00:01:37,810 --> 00:01:38,692
Everyone.

39
00:01:38,712 --> 00:01:41,744
Nobody else on Earth makes a box like this.

40
00:01:41,764 --> 00:01:46,464
Jensen spent thirty-three years turning a video game chip company into the one

41
00:01:46,484 --> 00:01:50,156
supplier every AI lab on the planet is queuing for.

42
00:01:50,176 --> 00:01:52,248
China's labs are in that queue too,

43
00:01:52,268 --> 00:01:55,731
with plenty of money and some of the best engineers in the world.

44
00:01:55,751 --> 00:01:57,823
Why doesn't China just make its own?

45
00:01:57,843 --> 00:02:1,175
Because it can't buy the machines that print the best chips.

46
00:02:1,195 --> 00:02:3,287
Huawei, China's champion,

47
00:02:3,307 --> 00:02:7,719
could make two hundred thousand AI chips in all of twenty twenty-five,

48
00:02:7,739 --> 00:02:9,211
and slower ones at that.

49
00:02:9,231 --> 00:02:11,471
And the gap is bigger than it sounds.

50
00:02:11,491 --> 00:02:14,469
How many of ours make one of theirs?

51
00:02:14,489 --> 00:02:14,835
Four.

52
00:02:14,855 --> 00:02:17,195
And how many of theirs for a top model?

53
00:02:17,215 --> 00:02:18,562
Fifty thousand.

54
00:02:18,582 --> 00:02:20,713
Then we buy theirs.

55
00:02:20,733 --> 00:02:22,004
We're not allowed.

56
00:02:22,024 --> 00:02:26,108
That's DeepSeek's real math, and the engineer is right about the last part.

57
00:02:26,128 --> 00:02:31,612
Since October twenty twenty-two, America has banned Nvidia's best chips for China.

58
00:02:31,632 --> 00:02:34,896
Jensen fought that ban for years, in public,

59
00:02:34,916 --> 00:02:37,325

60
00:02:37,345 --> 00:02:41,152
We went from ninety-five percent market share to zero percent.

61
00:02:41,172 --> 00:02:43,984
So China has the money and the engineers.

62
00:02:44,004 --> 00:02:47,316
What it doesn't have is a legal way to buy the box.

63

And the first people to get around that never touched a box at all.

64
00:02:51,020 --> 00:02:54,190
They carried one card at a time.

65

The first smuggler on our route drives a Prius.

66
00:02:58,377 --> 00:03:3,709
In Arizona, a man known as the Plug keeps a battery-powered test bench in the trunk,

67
00:03:3,729 --> 00:03:7,721

68
00:03:7,741 --> 00:03:10,113
There's also a spare license plate back there.

69
00:03:10,133 --> 00:03:11,711
Nobody asked about the plate.

70
00:03:11,731 --> 00:03:13,624
Your post said two thousand?

71
00:03:13,644 --> 00:03:14,576
Two thousand.

72
00:03:14,596 --> 00:03:15,638
If it runs.

73
00:03:15,658 --> 00:03:16,881
Where's it going?

74
00:03:16,901 --> 00:03:18,755
Somewhere it's worth more.

75
00:03:18,775 --> 00:03:20,059
And what do you make on it?

76
00:03:20,079 --> 00:03:21,499
Less than you'd think.

77
00:03:21,519 --> 00:03:23,708
You still owe me for the last batch!

78
00:03:23,728 --> 00:03:26,100
The Plug buys top gaming cards,

79
00:03:26,120 --> 00:03:29,632
the kind China's repair shops turn into cheap AI cards,

80
00:03:29,652 --> 00:03:34,216
and clears just under three hundred dollars on each one, before gas.

81
00:03:34,236 --> 00:03:36,668
That's the riskiest job in the whole chain,

82
00:03:36,688 --> 00:03:39,352
for what a waiter makes on one good Saturday.

83
00:03:39,372 --> 00:03:42,229
How do you smuggle a whole AI industry?

84
00:03:42,249 --> 00:03:44,022
Like ants moving house.

85
00:03:44,042 --> 00:03:44,723
Meaning?

86
00:03:44,743 --> 00:03:45,967
One crumb at a time.

87
00:03:45,987 --> 00:03:50,211
That's what the trade is called in Chinese: thousands of little trips,

88
00:03:50,231 --> 00:03:52,483
every one of them too small to notice.

89
00:03:52,503 --> 00:03:56,195
Students buy a graphics card at Best Buy, pack it in their luggage,

90
00:03:56,215 --> 00:03:58,499

91
00:03:58,519 --> 00:04:0,053
Anything to declare?

92
00:04:0,073 --> 00:04:1,200
Homework.

93
00:04:1,220 --> 00:04:2,431
Study hard.

94
00:04:2,451 --> 00:04:4,283
Some ants get creative.

95
00:04:4,303 --> 00:04:5,723
In twenty twenty-two,

00:04:5,743 --> 00:04:10,923

00:04:10,943 --> 00:04:13,125

98
00:04:13,145 --> 00:04:16,008
And once the cards arrive, nobody hides them.

99
00:04:16,028 --> 00:04:17,984
Is this the black market?

It's a shopping mall.

101
00:04:19,102 --> 00:04:20,827
So where are the smugglers?

102
00:04:20,847 --> 00:04:21,899
Upstairs.

103
00:04:21,919 --> 00:04:23,049
Doing inventory.

104
00:04:23,069 --> 00:04:28,593
Up there, the cartons are stacked a dozen high, five or six graphics cards in each,

105
00:04:28,613 --> 00:04:29,885

106
00:04:29,905 --> 00:04:31,005
Across town,

107
00:04:31,025 --> 00:04:33,725
one repair shop alone fixes up to five

108
00:04:33,745 --> 00:04:36,205
hundred of Nvidia's banned data-center chips

109
00:04:36,225 --> 00:04:39,729

110
00:04:39,749 --> 00:04:41,961
Nobody meets a man in a dark alley.

111
00:04:41,981 --> 00:04:43,179
They just have it shipped.

112
00:04:43,199 --> 00:04:48,205
Jensen heard about the ants for years, and he always laughed.

113
00:04:48,225 --> 00:04:51,657
Nvidia's chips are not little tiny potato chips.

114
00:04:51,677 --> 00:04:54,207
These are two tons.

115
00:04:54,344 --> 00:04:59,376
Every so often somebody says, you know, these GPUs are being smuggled.

116
00:04:59,396 --> 00:05:1,064
I really would love to see it.

117
00:05:1,084 --> 00:05:2,296
And he was right.

118
00:05:2,316 --> 00:05:7,460
A student can carry a card, but nobody carries a two-ton rack through an airport,

119
00:05:7,480 --> 00:05:11,352

120
00:05:11,372 --> 00:05:14,724
Ants can't move two hundred and forty thousand chips.

121
00:05:14,744 --> 00:05:16,636
For that you don't need a smuggler.

122
00:05:16,656 --> 00:05:18,347
You need a customer.

123
00:05:18,348 --> 00:05:20,520
Three hundred dollars a card.

00:05:20,540 --> 00:05:22,301
I need a better side job.

00:05:22,321 --> 00:05:23,553
Funny you say that.

00:05:23,573 --> 00:05:25,977
You've been watching one for five minutes.

127
00:05:25,997 --> 00:05:27,054
The cartoon?

128
00:05:27,074 --> 00:05:28,014
This video.

129
00:05:28,034 --> 00:05:31,090
The script, the voices, that Prius.

130
00:05:31,110 --> 00:05:36,254
Every shot and every sound effect, from a topic to a finished four K film,

131
00:05:36,274 --> 00:05:37,009
overnight.

132
00:05:37,029 --> 00:05:40,921
We make every video on this channel with a studio called Overnight.

133
00:05:40,941 --> 00:05:43,698
And they've just opened the app they use to the public.

134
00:05:43,718 --> 00:05:45,130
You give it an idea.

Your own Claude researches it, writes it, voices it,

137
00:05:53,153 --> 00:05:55,145
So I could make this.

00:05:55,165 --> 00:05:56,137
Myself.

139
00:05:56,157 --> 00:05:57,510
At this quality.

140
00:05:57,530 --> 00:05:58,240
Yes.

141
00:05:58,260 --> 00:05:59,351
With the charts?

142
00:05:59,371 --> 00:06:0,146
Yes.

143
00:06:0,166 --> 00:06:1,122
And the Prius?

144
00:06:1,142 --> 00:06:2,414
And the Prius.

145
00:06:2,434 --> 00:06:4,826
There are more than twenty-five styles in it.

146
00:06:4,846 --> 00:06:6,598
Money stories like this one.

147
00:06:6,618 --> 00:06:8,510
Three D news documentaries.

148
00:06:8,530 --> 00:06:10,282
Three D cartoon Shorts.

149
00:06:10,302 --> 00:06:11,574
Minecraft Shorts.

It's usually a hundred twenty-seven dollars a month.

00:06:14,546 --> 00:06:18,930
Right now it's seventy-seven, and the price goes up as more people join.

Whatever you join at stays yours.

And at three hundred members, Overnight closes the doors to the public again.

00:06:25,425 --> 00:06:28,403
Nobody wants the internet flooded with these.

155
00:06:28,423 --> 00:06:29,283
Three hundred.
