00:06:29,303 --> 00:06:29,846
Got it.

157
00:06:29,866 --> 00:06:32,898
Make fourteen videos in your first thirty days.

158
00:06:32,918 --> 00:06:35,729
If you're not happy with them, you get your first month back.

159
00:06:35,749 --> 00:06:37,521
made overnight dot com.

160
00:06:37,541 --> 00:06:40,505
It's on screen, and it's the first link in the description.

161
00:06:40,525 --> 00:06:42,229
Now, back to the box.

162
00:06:42,249 --> 00:06:43,801
It still needs a customer.

163
00:06:43,821 --> 00:06:49,123
And in June of twenty twenty-three, one opens for business in Shanghai.

164
00:06:50,776 --> 00:06:52,580
June, twenty twenty-three.

165
00:06:52,600 --> 00:06:57,172
A new company opens in Shanghai, called Shanghai Century Litong.

166
00:06:57,192 --> 00:07:0,306
Four months later, it's an official Nvidia partner.

167
00:07:0,326 --> 00:07:1,838
Not just any partner.

168
00:07:1,858 --> 00:07:6,359
A preferred cloud partner, with priority access to Nvidia's chips.

169
00:07:6,379 --> 00:07:7,978
Where does this go?

170
00:07:7,998 --> 00:07:9,550
Preferred Nvidia partner.

171
00:07:9,570 --> 00:07:11,186
We just got the chairs.

172
00:07:11,206 --> 00:07:12,534
Then hang it over the chairs.

173
00:07:12,554 --> 00:07:16,746
The first name tied to that company belongs to a woman called Huang Yu.

174
00:07:16,766 --> 00:07:18,778
Her sister is Alice Huang.

175
00:07:18,798 --> 00:07:21,930
You've met Alice: she ran Megaspeed in Singapore,

176
00:07:21,950 --> 00:07:26,662
and American spies watched her sit beside Jensen for a year without warning him.

177
00:07:26,682 --> 00:07:27,854
We told you that story.

178
00:07:27,874 --> 00:07:30,926
What we didn't tell you is who walked her to the table.

179
00:07:30,946 --> 00:07:32,090
It was her husband.

180
00:07:32,110 --> 00:07:35,882
Kang Wei is a fifty-one-year-old fund manager in Shanghai,

181
00:07:35,902 --> 00:07:38,054
on the board of a state-controlled bank.

182
00:07:38,074 --> 00:07:41,654
In the twenty-tens he invested in video game companies,

183
00:07:41,674 --> 00:07:43,594
which is how he came to know Jensen.

184
00:07:43,614 --> 00:07:46,903
Every game I invest in runs on your chips.

185
00:07:46,923 --> 00:07:49,167
Then you're my favorite investor.

186
00:07:49,187 --> 00:07:50,975
And he made the introduction.

187
00:07:50,995 --> 00:07:53,127
Jensen, this is my wife.

188
00:07:53,147 --> 00:07:53,917
Alice.

189
00:07:53,937 --> 00:07:55,544
Any friend of Kang's!

190
00:07:55,564 --> 00:07:57,279
We should do business.

191
00:07:57,299 --> 00:07:58,979
Then welcome to the table!

192
00:07:58,999 --> 00:08:2,051
For two years after that, Kang talked openly

193
00:08:2,071 --> 00:08:3,983
about how close the two of them were.

194
00:08:4,003 --> 00:08:5,691
He even had a joke for it.

195
00:08:5,711 --> 00:08:6,623
My wife?

196
00:08:6,643 --> 00:08:8,771
She's Jensen's personal assistant.

197
00:08:8,791 --> 00:08:11,463
Why would a partner badge matter more than money?

198
00:08:11,483 --> 00:08:15,035
Because Nvidia's chips are the hottest restaurant in town.

199
00:08:15,055 --> 00:08:16,467
Anyone can pay for dinner.

200
00:08:16,487 --> 00:08:18,578
Tonight's tables go to the regulars.

201
00:08:18,598 --> 00:08:20,653
Why is this line so long?

202
00:08:20,673 --> 00:08:22,025
Everybody has money.

203
00:08:22,045 --> 00:08:23,362
Nobody has chips.

204
00:08:23,382 --> 00:08:24,311
Who's she?

205
00:08:24,331 --> 00:08:25,208
A regular.

206
00:08:25,228 --> 00:08:26,808
Preferred partner.

207
00:08:26,828 --> 00:08:27,951
In four months.

208
00:08:27,971 --> 00:08:29,399
Is that fast?

209
00:08:29,419 --> 00:08:30,651
We make friends.

210
00:08:30,671 --> 00:08:32,423
So was it blackmail?

211
00:08:32,443 --> 00:08:32,895
No.

212
00:08:32,915 --> 00:08:37,599
Blackmail is for people who say no, and Jensen never had a reason to say no.

213
00:08:37,619 --> 00:08:42,535
She was a customer paying full price, a friend, and then more than a friend.

214
00:08:42,555 --> 00:08:44,600
She never threatened him once.

215
00:08:44,620 --> 00:08:46,347
Then what's this?

216
00:08:46,367 --> 00:08:47,322
His trust.

217
00:08:47,342 --> 00:08:49,250
And what did she pull with it?

218
00:08:49,270 --> 00:08:50,347
Her place in line.

219
00:08:50,367 --> 00:08:51,629
Did he ever feel it?

220
00:08:51,649 --> 00:08:52,843
He never saw the collar.

221
00:08:52,863 --> 00:08:56,315
He thought he was doing favors for a customer he cared about.

222
00:08:56,335 --> 00:08:59,267
Every love letter he sent her was a purchase order,

223
00:08:59,287 --> 00:09:1,319
and he never knew who she worked for.

224
00:09:1,339 --> 00:09:2,918
The President said so himself.

225
00:09:2,938 --> 00:09:7,131
He had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.

226
00:09:7,151 --> 00:09:8,983
Now our box has a buyer.

227
00:09:9,003 --> 00:09:11,853
Next it needs an address.

228
00:09:13,145 --> 00:09:18,169
On paper, a fifth of everything Nvidia sold in a year went to Singapore,

229
00:09:18,189 --> 00:09:20,861
an island a little smaller than New York City.

230
00:09:20,881 --> 00:09:25,780
That's twenty-four billion dollars of chips, billed to one small island.

231
00:09:25,800 --> 00:09:27,602
All of that went here?

232
00:09:27,622 --> 00:09:28,220
To the bill.

233
00:09:28,240 --> 00:09:29,330
And the chips?

234
00:09:29,350 --> 00:09:30,648
Under two percent.

235
00:09:30,668 --> 00:09:32,506
So where's the rest?

236
00:09:32,526 --> 00:09:33,368
Read the label.

237
00:09:33,388 --> 00:09:35,848
Nvidia's own annual report says it's

238
00:09:35,868 --> 00:09:38,380
perfectly normal: "Customers use Singapore to

239
00:09:38,400 --> 00:09:42,912
centralize invoicing while our products are almost always shipped elsewhere." Big

240
00:09:42,932 --> 00:09:47,364
companies pay their bills from one head office and ship to stores everywhere.

241
00:09:47,384 --> 00:09:50,394
It also makes Singapore the perfect first sticker.

242
00:09:50,414 --> 00:09:54,384
Our box is billed to Megaspeed, Alice's company in Singapore.

243
00:09:54,404 --> 00:09:55,806
Bill it to Singapore.

244
00:09:55,826 --> 00:09:57,076
And ship it to?

245
00:09:57,096 --> 00:09:57,918
Next door.

246
00:09:57,938 --> 00:10:2,022
Next door is Johor, in Malaysia, just across the causeway,

247
00:10:2,042 --> 00:10:5,467
where there's room and power for giant data centers.

248
00:10:5,487 --> 00:10:8,699
Malaysia doesn't sound like an AI superpower.

249
00:10:8,719 --> 00:10:13,563
But measured by the AI computing delivered there, it ranks fourth in the world,

250
00:10:13,583 --> 00:10:16,175
behind only America, China and Europe.

251
00:10:16,195 --> 00:10:20,767
Two of the ten most powerful AI data centers on Earth are Malaysian.

252
00:10:20,787 --> 00:10:24,099
And Johor boomed on a rule, not a crime.

253
00:10:24,119 --> 00:10:28,091
A Chinese company isn't allowed to own Nvidia's best chips,

254
00:10:28,111 --> 00:10:30,180
but it is allowed to rent them.

255
00:10:30,200 --> 00:10:33,609
China can't buy the chip, but it can rent it?

256
00:10:33,629 --> 00:10:34,695
From next door.

257
00:10:34,715 --> 00:10:37,142
Like a car you're not allowed to own...

258
00:10:37,162 --> 00:10:38,262
But you can drive it.

259
00:10:38,282 --> 00:10:39,161
From your couch.

260
00:10:39,181 --> 00:10:41,073
Renting has one catch.

261
00:10:41,093 --> 00:10:46,026
The chips are over there, and the data that trains an AI is still in China.

262
00:10:46,046 --> 00:10:47,321
The chips are in Malaysia.

263
00:10:47,341 --> 00:10:48,599
Our data is here.

264
00:10:48,619 --> 00:10:50,279
Eighty terabytes.

265
00:10:50,299 --> 00:10:52,425
The internet's too slow.

266
00:10:52,445 --> 00:10:53,311
Then fly it there.

267
00:10:53,331 --> 00:10:54,475
In suitcases.

268
00:10:54,495 --> 00:10:56,192
Why not one big one?

269
00:10:56,212 --> 00:10:58,608
Last year one heavy bag got noticed.

270
00:10:58,628 --> 00:11:1,040
So in March twenty twenty-five,

271
00:11:1,060 --> 00:11:6,720
four Chinese engineers flew from Beijing to Kuala Lumpur and trained an AI on three

272
00:11:6,740 --> 00:11:9,106
hundred rented Nvidia servers.

273
00:11:9,126 --> 00:11:10,759
Anything to declare?

274
00:11:10,779 --> 00:11:12,297
Hard drives.

275
00:11:12,317 --> 00:11:13,366
How many?

276
00:11:13,386 --> 00:11:14,360
Fifteen.

277
00:11:14,380 --> 00:11:15,124
Each?

278
00:11:15,144 --> 00:11:16,875
We're very organized.

279
00:11:16,895 --> 00:11:19,647
Then came the moment it could all have ended.

280
00:11:19,667 --> 00:11:24,181
Nvidia sent its own people to Malaysia to check on Megaspeed's chips.

281
00:11:24,201 --> 00:11:25,933
And that's the last one.

282
00:11:25,953 --> 00:11:26,819
All there?

283
00:11:26,839 --> 00:11:28,112
Every one.

284
00:11:28,132 --> 00:11:28,892
Told you.

285
00:11:28,912 --> 00:11:31,224
Every chip they checked was where it should be.

286
00:11:31,244 --> 00:11:34,368
Of course it was: a rented chip never has to leave.

287
00:11:34,388 --> 00:11:36,328
But add up the export papers,

288
00:11:36,348 --> 00:11:40,026
and four in ten of Megaspeed's chips aren't on them at all.

289
00:11:40,046 --> 00:11:42,198
And our box doesn't stay.

290
00:11:42,218 --> 00:11:45,782
From Johor it goes on to Shanghai, to Century Litong.

291
00:11:45,802 --> 00:11:50,606
And a box that leaves has a problem: on paper it's still sitting in Malaysia,

292
00:11:50,626 --> 00:11:54,116
and sooner or later somebody comes to count it.

293
00:11:55,458 --> 00:11:58,238
So how do you show an inspector a warehouse

294
00:11:58,258 --> 00:12:0,535
full of servers that already left?

295
00:12:0,555 --> 00:12:3,647
Another crew in the same trade worked out the answer.

296
00:12:3,667 --> 00:12:5,459
It starts at Super Micro,

297
00:12:5,479 --> 00:12:10,471
an American company that builds servers around Nvidia's chips, and its co-founder,

298
00:12:10,491 --> 00:12:11,398
Wally Liaw.

299
00:12:11,418 --> 00:12:12,918
Over two years,

300
00:12:12,938 --> 00:12:15,318
one company in Southeast Asia bought two

301
00:12:15,338 --> 00:12:18,038
and a half billion dollars of Super Micro's

302
00:12:18,058 --> 00:12:18,881
servers.

303
00:12:18,901 --> 00:12:20,713
Two and a half billion?

304
00:12:20,733 --> 00:12:22,312
Who is this customer?

305
00:12:22,332 --> 00:12:25,311
The eleventh most profitable one Super Micro had.

306
00:12:25,331 --> 00:12:27,639
Right next to America's cloud giants.

307
00:12:27,659 --> 00:12:29,374
Where did it keep them all?

308
00:12:29,394 --> 00:12:30,013
It didn't.

309
00:12:30,033 --> 00:12:32,705
Why would a server maker want orders like that?

310
00:12:32,725 --> 00:12:34,457
It's the line for chips again.

311
00:12:34,477 --> 00:12:36,040
I need bigger orders.

312
00:12:36,060 --> 00:12:38,309
We have nowhere to put them.

313
00:12:38,329 --> 00:12:39,675
That's not the point.

314
00:12:39,695 --> 00:12:43,496
Big orders are the only way Nvidia promises us the next chips.

315
00:12:43,516 --> 00:12:47,720
The servers went to Taiwan, then to the company in Southeast Asia,

316
00:12:47,740 --> 00:12:50,472
then on to China in unmarked boxes.

317
00:12:50,492 --> 00:12:55,176
In one stretch of three weeks, half a billion dollars of them crossed over,

318
00:12:55,196 --> 00:12:56,988
more than a jumbo jet's worth.

319
00:12:57,008 --> 00:13:0,263
Which left a warehouse that, on paper, was full.

320
00:13:0,283 --> 00:13:4,830
In August twenty twenty-five, Super Micro's own auditors were coming.

321
00:13:4,850 --> 00:13:6,670
The auditors come next week.

322
00:13:6,690 --> 00:13:8,547
The servers are already gone.

323
00:13:8,567 --> 00:13:10,517
Then we build new ones.

324
00:13:10,537 --> 00:13:11,689
Out of what?

325
00:13:11,709 --> 00:13:12,621
Boxes.

326
00:13:12,641 --> 00:13:15,473
The real boxes, with the real labels.

327
00:13:15,493 --> 00:13:16,924
And a hundred people.

328
00:13:16,944 --> 00:13:18,338
And forklifts?

329
00:13:18,358 --> 00:13:19,549
And forklifts.

330
00:13:19,569 --> 00:13:20,601
And they did.

331
00:13:20,621 --> 00:13:25,225
Dummy servers, packed in the maker's real boxes under its real labels.

332
00:13:25,245 --> 00:13:28,537
The broker's own estimate for the job was a hundred people,

333
00:13:28,557 --> 00:13:30,189
forklift drivers included.

334
00:13:30,209 --> 00:13:32,337
That's a lot of servers.

335
00:13:32,357 --> 00:13:33,982
Every single one.

336
00:13:34,002 --> 00:13:36,371
And where's our compliance officer?

337
00:13:36,391 --> 00:13:37,062
Busy.

338
00:13:37,082 --> 00:13:38,914
Busy is one word for it.

339
00:13:38,934 --> 00:13:41,806
One of Super Micro's own compliance officers,

340
00:13:41,826 --> 00:13:46,330
the person whose job was to check this customer, spent that audit offsite,

341
00:13:46,350 --> 00:13:48,935
enjoying entertainment the customer paid for.

342
00:13:48,955 --> 00:13:50,319
How's the audit going?

343
00:13:50,339 --> 00:13:51,251
Perfectly.

344
00:13:51,271 --> 00:13:52,084
Have dessert.

345
00:13:52,104 --> 00:13:54,141
But Washington had noticed.

346
00:13:54,161 --> 00:13:57,233
Your customer is sending your servers to China.

347
00:13:57,253 --> 00:13:58,561
Hold every shipment.

348
00:13:58,581 --> 00:14:2,565
In December, Washington sent its own inspector to the warehouse,

349
00:14:2,585 --> 00:14:5,566
and this time the crew did something even better.

350
00:14:5,586 --> 00:14:7,458
They opened the dummy boxes,

351
00:14:7,478 --> 00:14:10,970
warmed the real serial-number stickers with a red hair dryer,

352
00:14:10,990 --> 00:14:13,702
peeled them off and stuck them onto the fakes.

353
00:14:13,722 --> 00:14:16,454
The most fought-over technology on Earth,

354
00:14:16,474 --> 00:14:19,569
and the last line of defense was a sticker.

355
00:14:19,589 --> 00:14:21,828
Peel it warm, or it tears.

356
00:14:21,848 --> 00:14:23,297
Like a price tag?

357
00:14:23,317 --> 00:14:25,313
Exactly like a price tag.

358
00:14:25,333 --> 00:14:27,324
Serial number matches.

359
00:14:27,344 --> 00:14:28,889
They always do.

360
00:14:28,909 --> 00:14:32,314
And after that inspection, Liaw called the customer back.

361
00:14:32,334 --> 00:14:34,234
The inspection went fine.

362
00:14:34,254 --> 00:14:35,258
Order more.

363
00:14:35,278 --> 00:14:37,709
We still have nowhere to put them.

364
00:14:37,729 --> 00:14:39,563
You still don't need anywhere.

365
00:14:39,583 --> 00:14:43,647
In March twenty twenty-six, the Justice Department charged Liaw,

366
00:14:43,667 --> 00:14:46,899
Super Micro's Taiwan sales manager and the broker.

367
00:14:46,919 --> 00:14:48,951
The sales manager is a fugitive.

368
00:14:48,971 --> 00:14:53,675
The next day, Super Micro's stock lost a third of its value.

369
00:14:53,695 --> 00:14:56,155
Singapore had already charged three men with

370
00:14:56,175 --> 00:14:58,635
lying to Dell and Super Micro about who

371
00:14:58,655 --> 00:14:59,804
their servers were for.

372
00:14:59,824 --> 00:15:2,482
And who did they say the servers were for?

373
00:15:2,502 --> 00:15:4,949
A company called Luxuriate Your Life.

374
00:15:4,969 --> 00:15:7,784
Is that a company or a scented candle?

375
00:15:7,804 --> 00:15:9,177
On paper, a company.

376
00:15:9,197 --> 00:15:11,009
Our box beats the count too.

377
00:15:11,029 --> 00:15:13,081
On paper, it's still in Johor.

378
00:15:13,101 --> 00:15:16,033
In real life, it's being unloaded in Shanghai,

379
00:15:16,053 --> 00:15:20,183
and the receipt riding with it is as long as your arm.

380
00:15:21,497 --> 00:15:24,909
A ban on selling something should mean nobody gets paid.

381
00:15:24,929 --> 00:15:27,191
Our box got everybody paid.

382
00:15:27,211 --> 00:15:28,243
Line one.

383
00:15:28,263 --> 00:15:29,161
Nvidia.

384
00:15:29,181 --> 00:15:30,121
Paid first.

385
00:15:30,141 --> 00:15:30,723
In full.

386
00:15:30,743 --> 00:15:33,362
For chips China isn't allowed to buy?

387
00:15:33,382 --> 00:15:34,681
It sold them to a partner.

388
00:15:34,701 --> 00:15:36,163
On paper, in Singapore.

389
00:15:36,183 --> 00:15:39,907
And on the day it was made, each of those was a normal sale.

390
00:15:39,927 --> 00:15:44,711
Line two, the server makers, got paid for building the box around the chips.

391
00:15:44,731 --> 00:15:46,868
Then the price starts climbing.

392
00:15:46,888 --> 00:15:48,900
Line three is the broker.

393
00:15:48,920 --> 00:15:50,260
Last year in China,

394
00:15:50,280 --> 00:15:55,392
a rack of Nvidia's newest chips went for four hundred and ninety thousand dollars,

395
00:15:55,412 --> 00:15:57,764
half again what it cost anywhere else.

396
00:15:57,784 --> 00:15:59,568
That half is the broker's.

397
00:15:59,588 --> 00:16:2,600
He's a ticket scalper outside a sold-out stadium,

398
00:16:2,620 --> 00:16:5,600
except the concert is artificial intelligence.

399
00:16:5,620 --> 00:16:9,132
Then the landlord in Johor collects the rent on the data hall.

400
00:16:9,152 --> 00:16:14,064
The lender that holds the whole Malaysian business as security belongs to Alibaba,

401
00:16:14,084 --> 00:16:16,776
which is also one of the companies renting the chips.

402
00:16:16,796 --> 00:16:17,936
And in Shenzhen,

403
00:16:17,956 --> 00:16:22,856
a repair shop charges up to two thousand eight hundred dollars to bring one banned

404
00:16:22,876 --> 00:16:24,210
card back to life.

405
00:16:24,230 --> 00:16:26,158
And the guy with the Prius?

406
00:16:26,178 --> 00:16:27,358
Three hundred dollars.

407
00:16:27,378 --> 00:16:28,374
Before gas.

408
00:16:28,394 --> 00:16:30,977
The Prius guy got the worst deal.

409
00:16:30,997 --> 00:16:33,571
The Prius guy always gets the worst deal.

410
00:16:33,591 --> 00:16:35,883
And what did all of this cost us?

411
00:16:35,903 --> 00:16:37,027
Full price.

412
00:16:37,047 --> 00:16:38,578
And what did we get?

413
00:16:38,598 --> 00:16:41,318
Two hundred and forty thousand chips.

414
00:16:41,338 --> 00:16:42,518
We make friends.

415
00:16:42,538 --> 00:16:46,110
Open the love letter now and there's no poem inside.

416
00:16:46,130 --> 00:16:49,177
Just invoices, every one of them paid in full.

417
00:16:49,197 --> 00:16:52,661
But there's one more line on this receipt, right at the bottom,

418
00:16:52,681 --> 00:16:54,952
and it's the one nobody expects.

419
00:16:54,972 --> 00:16:56,084
Line seven.

420
00:16:56,104 --> 00:16:57,903
The United States government?

421
00:16:57,923 --> 00:16:59,075
On the legal ones.

422
00:16:59,095 --> 00:17:1,141
Fifteen percent of a weaker chip.

423
00:17:1,161 --> 00:17:2,483
And the stronger one?

424
00:17:2,503 --> 00:17:3,305
Twenty-five.

425
00:17:3,325 --> 00:17:7,837
Since last year, Washington lets Nvidia sell some chips to China,

426
00:17:7,857 --> 00:17:9,949
as long as the Treasury gets its cut.

427
00:17:9,969 --> 00:17:11,892
It's a toll booth on the front door.

428
00:17:11,912 --> 00:17:15,104
But a toll only works if somebody drives through.

429
00:17:15,124 --> 00:17:20,468
America finally agreed to sell China the H200, legally, with its cut.

430
00:17:20,488 --> 00:17:24,468
Right now, six hundred thousand of them are stuck in Hong Kong,

431
00:17:24,488 --> 00:17:26,091
because China won't let them in.

432
00:17:26,111 --> 00:17:31,843
Six hundred thousand chips is three times everything Huawei could make in a year.

433
00:17:31,863 --> 00:17:35,995
Beijing is keeping them out because it wants its companies buying Huawei,

434
00:17:36,015 --> 00:17:40,675
and it has already told its biggest tech firms to stop ordering even a cut-down

435
00:17:40,695 --> 00:17:41,639
Nvidia chip.

436
00:17:41,659 --> 00:17:44,956
So America finally said yes...

437
00:17:44,976 --> 00:17:46,273
And China said no.

438
00:17:46,293 --> 00:17:47,747
To the legal ones.

439
00:17:47,767 --> 00:17:48,995
Only the legal ones.

440
00:17:49,015 --> 00:17:51,555
China blocks the chips America agreed to

441
00:17:51,575 --> 00:17:54,307
sell it, and keeps the ones America banned.

442
00:17:54,327 --> 00:17:56,599
And with that many people getting paid,

443
00:17:56,619 --> 00:17:59,371
somebody in Washington was supposed to stop it.

444
00:17:59,391 --> 00:18:2,241
That somebody has a name.

445
00:18:3,529 --> 00:18:8,341
The man who decides who goes on America's blacklist is the Commerce Secretary,

446
00:18:8,361 --> 00:18:9,412
Howard Lutnick.

447
00:18:9,432 --> 00:18:10,698
What's on that?

448
00:18:10,718 --> 00:18:12,170
The Entity List.

449
00:18:12,190 --> 00:18:16,389
Get on it, and nobody can sell you American tech without a license.

450
00:18:16,409 --> 00:18:18,197
And who signs it?

451
00:18:18,217 --> 00:18:18,826
Me.

452
00:18:18,846 --> 00:18:22,638
Megaspeed should have been the easiest name he ever wrote down.

453
00:18:22,658 --> 00:18:24,558
American inspectors had already walked

454
00:18:24,578 --> 00:18:27,118
through its sites in Johor and found Nvidia

455
00:18:27,138 --> 00:18:28,983
servers nobody had unpacked.

456
00:18:29,003 --> 00:18:30,254
Still in the wrapping.

457
00:18:30,274 --> 00:18:33,706
Then a senator asked Lutnick to investigate Megaspeed.

458
00:18:33,726 --> 00:18:37,710
That same month, Commerce added one more name to the Entity List.

459
00:18:37,730 --> 00:18:39,222
It wasn't Megaspeed.

460
00:18:39,242 --> 00:18:41,282
How many did they add after that?

461
00:18:41,302 --> 00:18:41,828
None.

462
00:18:41,848 --> 00:18:43,497
In thirteen months?

463
00:18:43,517 --> 00:18:44,378
Not one.

464
00:18:44,398 --> 00:18:49,210
Not even when a classified memo about Alice Huang landed on Lutnick's desk.

465
00:18:49,230 --> 00:18:52,362
What finally moved Washington was the newspaper.

466
00:18:52,382 --> 00:18:55,394
At the end of October the story broke:

467
00:18:55,414 --> 00:18:57,794
American intelligence had Alice Huang down as

468
00:18:57,814 --> 00:18:59,306
a Chinese spy.

469
00:18:59,326 --> 00:19:3,650
And once it was out, the door came off its hinges in two weeks.

470
00:19:3,670 --> 00:19:5,862
First, in the White House Situation Room,

471
00:19:5,882 --> 00:19:9,303
the Treasury Secretary asked Lutnick the obvious question.

472
00:19:9,323 --> 00:19:12,002
How come Megaspeed isn't on the entities list?

473
00:19:12,022 --> 00:19:13,154
I don't know.

474
00:19:13,174 --> 00:19:14,231
I'll look into it.

475
00:19:14,251 --> 00:19:16,129
I need to check with the president.

476
00:19:16,149 --> 00:19:18,461
Then the spy memo itself leaked,

477
00:19:18,481 --> 00:19:23,985
and then the number came out: seven and a half billion dollars of Nvidia chips,

478
00:19:24,005 --> 00:19:26,057
through her family's company in Shanghai.

479
00:19:26,077 --> 00:19:28,709
We told you about two billion dollars of chips.

480
00:19:28,729 --> 00:19:30,306
It was seven and a half.

481
00:19:30,326 --> 00:19:31,658
She's a spy.

482
00:19:31,678 --> 00:19:32,830
There's a memo.

483
00:19:32,850 --> 00:19:35,322
Seven and a half billion dollars.

484
00:19:35,342 --> 00:19:36,243
In two weeks.

485
00:19:36,263 --> 00:19:38,006
So who's looking into it now?

486
00:19:38,026 --> 00:19:41,254
The President answered that on the day the number came out.

487
00:19:41,274 --> 00:19:44,886
I know the FBI is looking into it, in terms of something else,

488
00:19:44,906 --> 00:19:46,625
and I think that he'll be in good shape.

489
00:19:46,645 --> 00:19:48,913
In terms of something else?

490
00:19:48,933 --> 00:19:50,018
He didn't say what.

491
00:19:50,038 --> 00:19:54,942
The FBI is on it, and the Justice Department now runs the Megaspeed case.

492
00:19:54,962 --> 00:19:55,834
But they're late.

493
00:19:55,854 --> 00:19:58,898
The chips are already in China, and so is she.

494
00:19:58,918 --> 00:20:1,110
Alice Huang is home in Beijing.

495
00:20:1,130 --> 00:20:5,699
When reporters asked China's foreign ministry about that, the answer was short.

496
00:20:5,719 --> 00:20:7,605
I'm not familiar with that.

497
00:20:7,625 --> 00:20:9,206
Anything to declare?

498
00:20:9,226 --> 00:20:9,918
Nothing.

499
00:20:9,938 --> 00:20:11,034
It's already here.

500
00:20:11,054 --> 00:20:13,846
Her husband has stopped making jokes.

501
00:20:13,866 --> 00:20:18,086
Since February, Kang Wei has been in the hands of the Shanghai police,

502
00:20:18,106 --> 00:20:19,960
over a stock-manipulation case.

503
00:20:19,980 --> 00:20:23,284
So the chips are in China, the spy is home,

504
00:20:23,304 --> 00:20:26,674
and somebody still has to pay the bill.

505
00:20:27,942 --> 00:20:30,640
Start with the man who never saw the label.

506
00:20:30,660 --> 00:20:35,584
On the eighth of November, Jensen Huang admitted he'd been unfaithful to his wife.

507
00:20:35,604 --> 00:20:40,388
Four days later, he resigned from the company he'd built for thirty-three years.

508
00:20:40,408 --> 00:20:41,860
We told that story too.

509
00:20:41,880 --> 00:20:44,092
He built the box everybody wanted,

510
00:20:44,112 --> 00:20:46,504
and he never knew where his friend was sending it.

511
00:20:46,524 --> 00:20:47,876
Nobody blackmailed him.

512
00:20:47,896 --> 00:20:48,928
Nobody had to.

513
00:20:48,948 --> 00:20:52,015
And the people who knew who Alice was never told him.

514
00:20:52,035 --> 00:20:53,727
The stock paid next.

515
00:20:53,747 --> 00:20:55,967
Nvidia hit a record of two hundred and

516
00:20:55,987 --> 00:20:58,127
thirty-nine dollars a share on the sixth of

517
00:20:58,147 --> 00:20:58,879
October.

518
00:20:58,899 --> 00:21:2,923
On the thirteenth of November, it closed at a hundred and sixty-three.

519
00:21:2,943 --> 00:21:7,347

take.

540
00:21:57,168 --> 00:21:59,042
So what happens next?

Everybody testifies.

Jensen before Thanksgiving, Lutnick on the tenth of December.

and that America should sell in the open and win the world.

00:22:28,791 --> 00:22:31,943

00:22:31,963 --> 00:22:34,795

A hundred and sixty thousand.

Nvidia.

Everywhere.
